## Chapter (2)

The discussion—may God honor you—regarding the **Images** <term>Images: "al-suwar," specifically referring here to the decans, which are three 10-degree segments within each zodiac sign, each represented by a symbolic figure.</term> is among the most difficult matters because the ancients encoded them to the best of their ability. However, I will use metaphors for you to explain what they have hidden. Whoever wishes to delve deeply into this subject should consult "**The Great Book of Images by Zosimos**" <note>Zosimus of Panopolis was a 3rd-century Greco-Egyptian alchemist and mystic whose works were highly influential in the medieval Islamic world.</note>, for he encompassed this entire matter.

Know, my brother, that the images that rise within the zodiac signs are of two types. The first consists of the images and their forty-eight parts that exist in the celestial sphere. These are the "imaginary images" formed by the outlines of the **fixed stars**. These are what you see imagined through the grouping or separation of the fixed stars, such as the images of the zodiac signs themselves, and other figures like the **Dog**, the **Bear**, the **Eagle**, the **Hen**, and others. These images shift and move from one zodiac sign to another; thus, this characteristic is not inherent to the nature of the sphere, particularly in the **Zodiac Belt** <term>Zodiac Belt: "mintaqat al-buruj," the path of the sun and planets.</term>, because they move one degree every hundred years. As for those images near the **poles**, their movement is not apparent even over thousands of years because they are close to the axis, meaning the path of their circular rotation is very narrow.

This is one type. The second type consists of the "imaginary images" mentioned by the **Indians** <note>This refers to the "Sphaera Indica," a system of decans that entered Arabic astrology through Persian and Indian sources, often featuring more exotic or anthropomorphic imagery than the Greek system.</note>, who said:
a) In the first face <term>Face: "Wajh," another term for a decan, the 10-degree subdivision of a sign.</term> of **Aries** rises a man with red eyes, a large body, and a steadfast heart.

He is arrogant in himself, wearing a large white cloak tied at his waist with a rope. He is angry, standing on one leg, and he is a guardian and protector.

In the second face, there rises a woman wearing a cloak and red garments. She has one leg, and her form resembles that of a horse. In her soul, she desires to go and seek clothes, jewelry, and children.

In the third face, there rises a tawny man with red hair. He is angry and stubborn, holding a wooden sword and a rod in his hand. He wears red clothes and is skilled in the **craft of iron** <note>The association with iron links this face to the planet Mars, which traditionally governs smiths and metalworkers.</note>. He desires to do good but is unable to do so. The same logic applies to the rest of the zodiac signs.

Know that they only imagined these things based on the natures of the planets and the signs. They said of the first face: "a man with red eyes and a steadfast heart" because it is the house of **Mars** and his face, and he is the indicator of redness, bravery, and boldness. The "large white cloak" comes from the exaltation of the **Sun** and its rays. His "anger" comes from the mixing of Mars with the Sun in this place through ire. His "standing on one leg" and his "guarding" are the actions of the servants of the ruling tyrants.

They said of the second face: "a woman" instead of a man because it is the term <term>Term: "Hadd," a further subdivision of a sign governed by a specific planet.</term> of **Mercury**, and Mercury is feminine for most of his time. Within it are also two degrees of the term of **Venus**. The "red clothes" are from the natures of Mars. Her having the "form of a horse" is from the natures of Mars the Cavalier, who indicates riding animals due to his strength in the sixth house <note>The sixth house in astrology is associated with small livestock and service animals.</note>, and among animals are the beasts of war. Her "seeking jewelry" is from the portion of the Sun, and "clothes" are because of the Sun's rays that veil her. "Children" are mentioned because the Midheaven <term>Midheaven: "Wast al-Sama," the highest point in the chart, associated here with light and the beginning of being.</term> is the house of light and the indicator of the beginning of existence.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of celestial influences, transitioning from the general actions of the spheres to the specific astrological and physical effects of the Moon’s phases. And they do not say, as we say, that its best state in relation to the Sun [is its opposition], for they believe that its best state in relation to the Sun is its being full of light. Thus, when it joins with the Sun <note>The "conjunction" or New Moon phase.</note>, they believe it only becomes stronger for it, not that it is its best state or the most powerful in its action. However, all of our ancients have agreed that the Moon’s best state in its formation, its distance from, and its proximity to the Sun is when it joins with the Sun in a single minute <term>Minute: A unit of angular measurement; here meaning the Moon and Sun are at the exact same degree and minute of the zodiac.</term>. This state in relation to the Sun is a **fifth state**, governed by a rule different from the other four. It is the most majestic of its states and the most powerful in its actions, because it rejoices in its meeting with the Sun, just as a traveler rejoices when returning from his journey to his homeland. At that time, it becomes the doer of things; even if it had performed parts of them previously, during the conjunction, it completes what was unfinished and adds what was lacking. They also say that it becomes capable of actions similar to the actions of the Sun, which is a great matter and a significant state. They said that at this time, "properties" <term>Properties (Khawass): Hidden or occult qualities of substances that produce specific effects, often considered the "spiritual" or chemical essence of a thing.</term> manifest in all composite bodies. It should not be understood from us here that the Moon creates these properties and other things, for all these actions belong to the Sun. Rather, the Moon’s role is to manifest those traces that the Sun has produced, bringing them out from their hiding places and igniting them after they have been extinguished—or we might say more generally that it reveals them after they were hidden. And how could it be said otherwise, when the Sun is the source of all things, bringing them from non-existence into being? These five states that we have described for the Moon in relation to the Sun correspond to all states of animals, plants, and minerals. (Similarly, the Moon’s state in relation to the Sun corresponds to the states of all animals in their ages: childhood, youth, maturity, old age, and decrepitude).

And its growth and expansion are more apparent, and this is most clear in what spreads across the Earth. It has a **second state** from after its first quarter until the time of its completion in light. Its completion in this regard is the time of its opposition <term>Opposition: The "Istiqbal," when the Moon is 180 degrees from the Sun, appearing as a Full Moon.</term> to the Sun, for it moves heat and moisture equally. During this time, it is most intense in the expansion and growth of all plants, and its action is most apparent in everything it does—moving moisture and heat in the bodies of animals, the tissues of plants, and in minerals. From the **opposition** until the time of its second halving of light <note>The waning half-moon or third quarter.</note>, it moves moisture and heat, though it moves moisture slightly less and heat slightly more. Thus, its effect on the bodies of animals, plants, and minerals is that it expands them, makes them grow, and moves them toward opening, spreading, and stretching, except that its expansion via heat is greater than that via moisture. From its **second halving** until its concealment by the Sun's rays, its action and its movement of heat are very, very slight—less than in the three preceding forms—to the point that it is said, by comparison, to dry slightly and cool significantly. This is because its movement of moisture is lessened; therefore, we say it is permissible to state that it cools greatly in this quarter and dries slightly.

And when it meets the Sun in a single minute, that is its **fifth state**. According to the **Chaldeans** <term>Chaldeans (al-Kasdaniyyun): Ancient inhabitants of Mesopotamia, often cited in medieval Arabic texts as the founders of agriculture and astral sciences.</term>, it is its best state and the most powerful for its action. According to the **Indians**, it is its most corrupt state and the weakest for its action and its powers. According to the **Persians**, its strength, weakness, and the increase or decrease of its action depend on the zodiac sign in which the conjunction with the Sun occurs. As for the **Greeks** and the **Egyptians**, they believe that its meeting with the Sun makes it stronger, as we have said.

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of the Moon's astrological influence. It moves from the Moon's specific relationship with the Sun to how the "Two Luminaries" (the Sun and Moon) and the planets cause constant change in the physical world of "Generation and Corruption." It specifically addresses how eclipses and planetary positions affect earthly life, such as plants and animals.</meta>

<margin>a</margin> For it receives constant change from the two luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> and the planets; it receives within itself goodness from good conditions and receives corruption from corrupt conditions. Eclipses are an occurrence <margin>3</margin> for the two luminaries and the planets that resembles the corruption of composite bodies <note>Physical objects made from the four elements: earth, water, air, and fire.</note>. No one should think that the two luminaries possess any corruption in their own essence, neither in terms of their occurrences nor their substances. <margin>b</margin> Our calling these afflictions "celestial" has a specific meaning: it is because the cause for their occurrence—and the occurrence of every affliction that happens to <margin>6</margin> animals, plants, and other bodies composed of the four elements—is the eclipse of the Moon and the eclipses of the planets.

Let us return to our subject and say: It is necessary in all actions to look <margin>c</margin> at the position of <margin>9</margin> the Moon, which is the most beneficial of things, the most truthful in its effects, and the most indicative of what occurs in the world of generation and corruption <note>The sublunary world; the earthly realm where things are born, change, and die.</note>, as it is the most specifically concerned with its governance. You must look at how <margin>12</margin> healthy it is from the "malefics" <note>Traditionally the planets Mars and Saturn, associated with challenges.</note> and its distance from the **Combust Path** <term>Combust Path (al-tariqa al-muhtaraqa): A specific section of the Zodiac (usually late Libra to early Scorpio) considered unlucky or debilitating for the Moon.</term>. For every action whose beginning was at a time of its safety and good rectitude, its outcome will be praiseworthy and its benefit complete. Its duration and stability will be according to the slowness or speed of its movement and what its indicators point toward. If it is <margin>15</margin> joined to the malefics, descending toward the South, or at the very end of a sign or in its first degree, and has not yet completed it, then that is bad. Or if it is in its "fall" <note>The sign where a planet's influence is weakest; for the Moon, this is Scorpio.</note>, or "void of course" from the lord of its house <note>Meaning it makes no astrological aspect to the planet that rules the sign it is currently in.</note>, not looking toward it, or falling away from a "pivot" <note>The four most powerful houses in an astrological chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th.</note>, or if it is with the **Tail** <term>The Tail (al-Dhanab): The South Node of the Moon, often associated with loss or diminishing influence in medieval astrology.</term> of the Dragon, then that beginning will have no stability.

<column-break/>

Likewise, it may correspond to the four seasons of the year, and it may correspond to the four directions which are called the "angles of the world," namely: the East, the West, the Right (South), and the Left (North). From these <margin>3</margin> four directions, four winds blow. All of these may correspond to the four humors <note>Blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> that are in the human body.

All of these meanings and these specific aspects—even if their origin is from the planets and the two luminaries <margin>6</margin> by the power of their movements—once they exist in this form, they receive from the powers of the movements of the planets things that are sent toward them. After being in their forms, they take on conditions that necessitate forms that are different from their initial forms. Since this is the case, all composite bodies undergo <margin>9</margin> constant changes according to what they receive from the powers of the movements of the planets and their correspondences with one another. These changes are those called "permanent partial changes." Those first ones we mentioned previously, which are the pillars and origins of things, are called the "fixed universal changes" of things, which do not cease nor <margin>12</margin> flip over. Were they to flip, the forms of all things would be corrupted; so they are the "fixed universals."

<margin>a</margin> The result of what we have presented is that all things—in their conditions, their beginnings, and their outcomes—correspond to the state of the Moon in relation to the Sun. This is because this accidental cause affecting the vineyards, the plants <margin>15</margin> entirely, and all composite bodies, comes from the stars, from the Moon specifically and from some of the planets generally. Those subsequent afflictions are produced by the eclipse of the Moon and the eclipses of the planets.

<margin>1</margin> is good and its companion <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign currently occupied by the Moon.</note> is "fallen" <note>In a cadent house, traditionally considered a weak or unlucky position.</note>, then the start of the work will be good, but its conclusion will be poor. Even if it is a malefic <note>A "challenging" planet, like Saturn or Mars.</note> but its position is favorable, then the most beneficial thing alongside that is for Jupiter or Venus to be in the Ascendant or aspecting <margin>6</margin> the Ascendant. That indicates the completion of the work, a good outcome, a swift benefit, and a general <margin>6</margin> blessing. This is particularly certain if the Moon is connecting to a benefic planet, provided that benefic is not "deficient" <note>Weakened by its position.</note> or retrograde. This is favorable for every task except for a slave who wishes to flee from his master or someone taking what does not belong to him.
<margin>9</margin> The Moon is the most entitled of the planets to govern what lies beneath it in the world of Generation <margin>9</margin> and Corruption <note>The earthly realm where things are born, change, and die.</note>. It acts as the mediator because it receives the influences of the other planets and delivers them to this earthly world. Therefore, you must first look at what I mentioned regarding its good or bad condition. Note <margin>12</margin> its increase at its beginning; from the moment it departs from the Sun, it begins to gain strength. It then changes at <margin>12</margin> its sextile <note>An angle of 60 degrees.</note>, its square <note>90 degrees</note>, its trine <note>120 degrees</note>, and its opposition <note>180 degrees</note> to the Sun. If it is the Lord of the Sixth House <note>The Sixth House traditionally governs illness, servants, and small animals.</note>, then the matter arises from enemies, slaves, diseases, thefts, small prisons, and four-legged livestock. If it is the Lord of the Twelfth House <note>The Twelfth House governs hidden enemies and confinement.</note>, it indicates that the corruption stems from misery, despair, enemies, and medium-sized prisons. Everything I am mentioning to you regarding these configurations is of no use in the great science of talismans <term>Talismans: Objects created at specific astrological moments to capture planetary influence (Arabic: *al-talasimat*).</term> unless you take the utmost care and ensure that the Ascendant is in a diurnal sign by day and a nocturnal sign by night, and that it is rising "straight" rather than "crooked" <note>Signs of "straight" or "long" ascension take longer to rise over the horizon and were considered more stable/favorable.</note>. Thus, by discerning the condition of the planets and what meanings they signify, you shall achieve your desire in this art. Whenever you desire love, friendship, or social connection, make the Moon "received" by Venus from a trine aspect, and it is best if this occurs in its House or Exaltation.

Know that the **Trine** is a gathering in the form of an equilateral triangle, where each of its sides consists of one hundred and twenty degrees of the encompassing sphere. The **Sextile** is a gathering in the form of an equilateral hexagon, where each of its sides consists of sixty degrees of the encompassing sphere. The **Square** is a gathering in the form of an equilateral square, where each of its sides consists of ninety degrees of the encompassing sphere. The aspect of **Opposition** is the "second square."

Let us return to our purpose and say: if circumstances occur where it is not possible for Venus to be the "receiver," then let it be in a trine aspect to the Moon, and let the Moon be received by Jupiter or by the Lord of its House, whether by trine, sextile, or conjunction. If that is difficult and cannot be arranged, then let the Moon be in one of the dignities of Venus, made fortunate by Jupiter and safe from the Malefics <note>The "Malefics" are Saturn and Mars, planets associated with obstacles and destruction.</note>.

Likewise, beware of the "falling" <note>Falling: Referring to planets in 'cadent' houses (3, 6, 9, 12), which were considered weak and unable to act effectively.</note> of the Lord of the need, the Two Luminaries, or the Lord of the Ascendant away from the "pivots" <note>Pivots: The four most powerful houses in a chart (1, 4, 7, 10), also known as Angles.</note>. If this proves difficult, <margin>15</margin> then look to the planet that is most prominent among the "Five Hylegs" <term>Five Hylegs: Five specific points in a birth chart (Sun, Moon, Ascendant, Part of Fortune, and the Prenatal Syzygy) used to determine life force.</term> and connect it with the planet most prominent in the meanings of the need. Make these two "received" and fortunate. Beware also of the affliction of the Lord of the Moon, the Lord of the Fourth, and the Lord of the Ascendant, for in that lies the affliction and corruption of the outcome of the need.

Whenever you wish to attempt any of the industrial crafts or their treatments, and things that return to the hand of the <margin>18</margin> artisan repeatedly, let that be while the Moon is in a "bicorporeal" sign <note>Bicorporeal signs: Also known as mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which represent change and flexibility.</note>, pure from the malefics. Let the Ascendant likewise be improved. If the attempt concerns gold, strengthen the Sun and improve it at the beginning of your work, and likewise in all its conditions.

Know that <gloss>b</gloss> the practitioners of the craft of talismans among the ancients believe that the quarters of the sphere move eight degrees forward <note>accession</note> and eight degrees backward <note>recession</note>. A group of those who follow the craft of astronomical tables <term>Zij: A set of astronomical tables used for calculating the positions of the sun, moon, and planets.</term> have neglected this in their calculations, yet there is great benefit in it for this craft—I mean

<column-break/>

the talismanic craft. The way to reach knowledge of this, as we have verified, is to learn the date of King Augustus. Take one hundred and twenty-eight years before King Augustus; for that was the end of the recession of those eight degrees at that time. Then was the beginning of their accession after that. Then you add three hundred and thirteen years to these years, from the beginning of King Augustus to the beginning of King Diocletian. You also add the years of Diocletian. After that, take one part for every eighty from the total; for it moves one degree in every eighty of these years. Whatever the total is, we cast out eights <note>A mathematical operation, likely modulo 8.</note> and whatever remains, we add to the calculation of the Sun, the Moon, and the five wandering stars <note>The five planets known to the ancients: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.</note>. By this, you will reach the works you seek in this craft. Do not neglect the matter of the accession and recession of the sphere, for it is the pillar in the matter of talismans regarding the images <note>Referring to the specific forms or symbols engraved on talismans.</note>. Know this, for it is one of their hidden secrets. These eight degrees of accession and recession are completed every six hundred and forty years. I have already informed you where the recession ended, and by that, you will know the time of its accession and recession. There is also a dire need for it in the science of effects. This accession and recession come from the movement of the pole of the zodiacal sphere, and the movement is from East to West or from West to East—nothing else is correct but these two ways. When it begins to approach [accession], it indicates events that will occur in the world, and likewise, when it begins to recede [recession], it indicates other events that occurred due to the cause of accession and recession. Know also that these belong to the zodiacal sphere, not the right sphere <note>The 'right sphere' refers to the celestial equator.</note>.

## Chapter (5)

I have seen, regarding a leader among the predecessors in this craft, wonders on this subject that I thought I should recount. Among these is that he divided this science into three parts:

The first is the **science of talismans**. He considered the nation most concerned with this to be the Sabians <note>A group often identified in Islamic tradition as star-worshippers from Harran, credited with preserving Hermetic and Neoplatonic knowledge.</note>, who are the subjects of the Nabataeans among the Chaldeans.

The second is the **science of the stars**, including performing offerings, incense, and rituals for them. The people of Greece stood alone in this second type, yet they were also superior in the foundation of both, which is the science of the stars—the foremost and most virtuous science.

The third is the **science of "qalqatiriyyat"** <note>original: "al-qalqatiriyyat" — a technical term likely referring to specialized incantations or alchemical-magical operations</note> and charms through pure, effective, and serious resolve, as well as the knowledge of the spirits who are subject to it and the submission <gloss>to</gloss> those words through correspondence. This science was the specialty of the Indians, who devoted themselves to it, as did the Sakasak of Yemen and the Copts of Egypt, who were well-established in it. Each of these sciences has a foundation and both theoretical and practical introductions.

It is well-known regarding the people of India that they possess effective and successful incantations against deadly poisons without the use of medicine. They possess words by which they strike people down, and upon hearing them, the mind is altered; they can even kill by their movement. Among their various types of music, they have an instrument they call the *Kankala* <note>A one-stringed Indian instrument, often associated with ascetic practitioners.</note>. It has a single string on a single body, through which one can imitate any desired sound and subtle...

Know, may God honor you, that the reality of the **dream** is the representation of individual things stripped of their physical vessels. It occurs when the soul ceases to use the senses and instead employs thought. This happens because the <term>Imaginative Power [al-quwwah al-mutakhayyilah]</term> <note>In medieval Islamic psychology, this power sits between the external senses and the intellect, capable of manipulating images stored in the memory.</note> combines the impressions of sensible objects it finds within itself and separates them from one another. It has a third function, which is **imitation** <note>original: "al-muhakah" — the ability of the imagination to create symbols or metaphors for abstract ideas.</note>. 

If the **Rational Soul** is at its peak of perfection, the dreamer sees the thing and it manifests exactly as it is. However, if the Imaginative Power is more dominant, the dream manifests as a symbolic meaning. For example, in a perfect soul, one might see a dog or a predator attacking him, and it happens exactly as seen. But if the Imaginative Power is the one at work, it might manifest as a <term>guard [shurti]</term> or a thief; this is a representation of the "meaning." 

If the physical nature is strong and the soul is occupied by it—due to its power over sexual desire, clothing, and everything one is busy with while awake—this appears in the dream as an obsession with pleasures and "swimming" in them. For instance, if one is preoccupied with intercourse due to the fullness of his body <note>Referring to an excess of "humors" or fluids in the body, a common medieval medical explanation for physical urges.</note>, he will have a wet dream. If his body is filled with **moisture**, he will see water and rivers in his sleep. If **cold and dryness** <note>The melancholic humor.</note> dominate his temperament, he sees terrifying and frightening things. If his temperament is **choleric and hot** <note>The bilious humor.</note>, he sees fires, ovens, and similar things. 

Know this, just as the reality of <term>Augury [al-zajr]</term> <note>Divination based on the flight or cries of birds or other spontaneous signs.</note> is actually **physiognomy**. This occurs after reflecting on the matter being divined, whether through an example one looks at or something heard while in a state of reflection, as the Imaginative Power is sent forth to look for the knowledge it seeks. If the Imaginative Power is strong, the matter is pictured for the person like someone looking into a polished mirror. He seeks help from what he has seen and heard, which leads him to a certain kind of knowledge. This is how the Imaginative Power acts when the senses are at rest: it mediates between the sensible things seen while awake and combines them with the intelligible, resulting in...

# The Hierarchy of Planetary Influence and the Science of Talismans

<page-num>93</page-num>
<page-num>92</page-num>

The way of every planet that conjoins with Saturn is that it falls under Saturn's influence. This is because Saturn's power is stronger than the powers of all the wandering planets <note>the five planets known to the ancients—Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—which appear to "wander" against the fixed stars</note> because of the conditions we have mentioned. This is either due to its great height or its proximity to the two great spheres of the universe—the Aether <note>the fifth element, or quintessence, which makes up the heavens</note> and the sphere of the Fixed Stars—or due to the slowness of its travel and its strong similarity to the Aetherial sphere of the universe, and other such reasons. In all that is said regarding such conjunctions, it is held that if Jupiter, the Sun, or Venus mix their actions with Saturn,
<margin>6</margin> they change it completely and improve it to some extent. The same applies to the fixed stars when they are associated with Jupiter. This matter continues to flow in a single, consistent, and unchanging order down to the Moon; thus, its actions are realized in the spheres of Fire and Air, and the actions of Fire and Air are realized
<margin>9</margin> in the spheres of Water and Earth. The actions of these four elements then become effective in the generation <note>the process of physical birth and coming-into-being</note> that arises from them.
It is possible for any two planets in conjunction to have three states: excessive, deficient, or intermediate between them. For instance, the Moon may be with Saturn, and its action falls under the action of
<margin>12</margin> Saturn—meaning Saturn's power [dominates]—and this occurs when they are in alignment, in exaltation <term>exaltation: a specific sign in the zodiac where a planet's influence is most potent</term>, in apogee <term>apogee: the point in a planet's orbit where it is furthest from the Earth</term>, and similar positions, provided the Moon and Saturn are on the same path in these specific places and nowhere else. The same applies to Saturn in all other positions and to all the planets.
<margin>15</margin> It is also possible for the action and power of the Moon to be much greater than the power of Saturn if the Moon is in those high positions while Saturn is in their opposites. If the Moon and Saturn are both in the opposites of those noble positions equally, then the action of the
<margin>18</margin> Moon follows the action of Saturn, just as in the first case. When Saturn is in those high positions and the Moon is in its own [lower] positions, the action of the Moon is entirely weak. When Saturn is in its direct path or in retrograde <note>the optical illusion where a planet appears to move backward in the sky</note>, and other such changes in the balanced paths of travel...

# The Nature of Celestial Motion and the Bestowal of Forms

<page-num>94</page-num>

The motion of every sphere toward what it contains of its own sub-spheres and planets is universal to those planets, spheres, and all their movements. Furthermore, the cause of the planets’ actions and the specific effects they possess by their very nature is 
<margin>3</margin> the movement of their spheres through them. This is because planets do not move by their own essence; they are moved <term>by accident</term> <note>original: "bi-l-'arad"; in medieval philosophy, this means something moved by the container it is in, like a passenger on a ship, rather than moving by its own power</note>. For this reason, the action of the sphere is twofold: motion by essence, and heat <term>by accident</term>, since heat is something that arises as a consequence of motion. 

Motion, as we have stated, is the existence of the sphere and the "Bestowal" <note>original: "al-'ata'"; the divine or celestial emanation of forms onto the material world</note>. This is what is 
<margin>6</margin> sought after in the science of talismans: the movement of a receptive object and its extraction from <term>potentiality</term> into <term>actuality</term>. Within the "Image" or "Form" is the likeness of everything, and within "Matter" is the receptivity to everything. Every matter has a form—that is, a temperament—and every form has a matter—that is, a temperament—upon which it is carried. An example of this is a small fire: 
<margin>9</margin> it grows and becomes great because the small fire extracts the fire that was in the <term>prime matter</term> <note>original: "al-hayula"; the formless underlying substance of the universe</note> in potentiality until it brings it into existence in its own right; thus it increases because it has become <term>actualized</term>.

Know that an opposite cannot enter upon that which is already actualized to corrupt it; rather, it enters upon 
<margin>12</margin> that which is in potentiality to corrupt it, not that which is actualized. Everything that follows the course of Nature is balanced, while whatever deviates from the course of Nature is imbalanced. Because of 
<margin>15</margin> this, that which is "hot in actuality" naturally moves that which is "hot in potentiality." When a hot thing provides 
<margin>15</margin> heat, it only does so through the principle and cause within it that has the power to heat. Just as that which is hot in actuality moves that which is hot in potentiality, so too is the "potentially hot" moved naturally by the "actually hot." For just as the former is the principle of action within its own self, the latter is the principle of 
<margin>18</margin> being acted upon within its own self. Know this well.

The two actions were nearly equal, especially if that coincided with the Moon being at its height. This is because the peak

<margin>3</margin> its state. However, the state of Saturn and Jupiter is not like that of Saturn and the Moon; they are nearly equal in most cases. When Saturn is high and Jupiter is also high, 
the action is stronger for Jupiter—unless Jupiter is high while Saturn is in 
<margin>6</margin> its middle course, at its exaltation, or in direct motion. In that case, the action does not belong to Jupiter alone. 
But if the opposite occurs, the action belongs to Saturn, and Jupiter’s action is entirely nullified, or at least diminished. Similarly, when Mars and Saturn are together, the actions are more apparent for Mars, 
<margin>9</margin> except under those same conditions previously mentioned. As for Venus and Mercury, they have a relationship and similarity to 
every planet. The Moon is not like them, for it has no relationship or similarity 
to the higher planets. This is a principle upon which the work is built, and it is among the things needed for these <term>accidental correspondences</term> 
<margin>12</margin> and is of the greatest necessity in the science of talismans.

Know that the actions of the planets are by their very essences because they are <term>simple</term> <note>original: "basit"; in medieval science, a simple substance is made of one thing and is not a mixture of elements</note>. That which is simple is not 
subject to corruption <note>decay or breaking down</note>. If a simple thing were to corrupt, it would cease to exist. 
<margin>15</margin> Corruption only occurs in compound things made of different components. Know that the action of the "Sphere of the Whole" <note>the outermost sphere of the universe which carries all others</note> in the East 
is the general action, in absolute terms, for all the spheres and all the planets. The reason for this is that it is 
the cause of their motion, yet it is in truth "Absolutely Still," because it is the mover of all the spheres. For this reason, 
<margin>18</margin> it is said to be the "Mover of the All," while it is not itself moving, as that would be an impossibility <note>an allusion to the Aristotelian "Unmoved Mover"</note>. 
As for the sphere of the Fixed Stars, although its motion is general, it is specific in relation 
to the motion of the Sphere of the Whole. The same applies to the rest of the spheres. You must know that...

### Chapter (7)

From what we have mentioned, one becomes aware of the form of "reception" and "bestowal" in the actions and works of talismans, 
<margin>3</margin> and the form of "similarity" and "difference." Similarity is a <term>category</term> <note>original: "maqula"; referring to the Aristotelian Categories used to classify all aspects of reality</note> in the work of talismans. 
This is because it is the similarity that exists through the work between the action of the planets and the action of the stone 
from which the talisman is made, [and] the time, the place, and the setting up of the talisman. For it is 
<margin>6</margin> by the combination of these things that the talisman exists, and by their absence, the talisman is nullified. Thus, "Relation" <note>original: "al-idafa"; the category of how things relate to one another</note> is one of the 
great principles in the existence of the talisman.

**Quantity** <note>original: "al-kamm"</note> is also like this, because quantity—as is said in the <term>Instructional Sciences</term> <note>original: "al-ta'alim"; usually referring to the quadrivium of mathematics, geometry, astronomy, and music</note>—is divided in its largest 
<margin>9</margin> division into two parts: the **Continuous** and the **Discrete**. The continuous part is divided into five 
parts: the line, the surface, the body, time, and place. The 
discrete part is divided into **speech** <note>original: "al-qawl"; or "statement"</note> and **number**. All of these divisions are required 
<margin>11</margin> and most urgently needed for the knowledge of the work of talismans. 

As for the **line**, it is for the sake of the <term>alignment</term> <note>original: "al-musamata"; the direct geometric or astronomical path between two points</note> occurring between 
the planets and the talisman, and for the sake of the alignment between the talisman and the object intended for the 
occurrence of the talisman’s action, through "likeness" and "opposition." These two parts into which 
<margin>15</margin> the line is divided regarding alignment are the "statement" that was mentioned in the *Instructional Sciences* regarding the **straight line**. 
Their statement regarding it is that "the straight line is that which is placed in opposition, whichever points are placed one upon 
the other." This is the most complete thing said regarding the nature of the talisman. That straight line is the thing upon 
<margin>18</margin> which the object carried upon it passes in a single path from the beginning of the point from which it emerges...

### Chapter (8)

Know that the arrangement of the "degrees of natures" <note>The hierarchy of elemental strengths used in medieval science</note> devised by the ancients only became clear to them through this path, 
until they knew the ranks of the powers of medicines, foods, and other things. Then, after that, they compounded them 
<margin>3</margin> with one another until the benefits of medicines and their various actions became apparent to them. It is necessary here to 
mention what is required of this knowledge. I say: the ancients differed regarding the 
**Simple Natures**—what they are—and they disputed their number. A group of them, who are the "Verifiers" <note>original: "al-muhaqqiqun"; those who seek the ultimate truth through rigorous proof</note>, said 
<margin>6</margin> that the Simple Natures and the **Primordial Mothers** <note>original: "al-ummahat al-awa’il"; a philosophical term for the four basic qualities</note> are: **Heat**, **Cold**, **Moisture**, 
and **Dryness**. In reality, these are qualities and simple first principles, and there is no disagreement on this. Then, 
they named the "compounds," which are our terms: **Hot**, **Cold**, **Moist**, and **Dry**. This is because when we say 
<margin>9</margin> "Hot," it refers to matter accompanied by "Heat," and the same applies to the rest. This is not the same as saying "Heat" 
and "Cold" and so on. After this composition, there is a second composition, which is our saying: **Hot-Dry**, 
**Hot-Moist**, **Cold-Dry**, and **Cold-Moist**. These are "secondary" in their composition because it has 
<margin>12</margin> become clear that they are not single units, since Heat is different from Dryness or Moisture—and the same is true 
for Cold paired with others. This composition is followed by a third composition, which is our saying: **Fire**, 
**Air**, **Water**, and **Earth**. These are a "third composition" in relation to the first simple principle 
<margin>15</margin> and the first and second compounds. Then follows the fourth composition, which is that found in 
individual bodies <note>original: "al-ashkhas"; specific physical entities or people</note>. This can be divided into parts: in the world, these are the **Four Seasons**, which are...

<margin>3</margin> I say that **Heat**, **Cold**, **Moisture**, and **Dryness** precede Fire, Air, Water, and Earth in many ways that are evident through both reasoning and the senses. One reason is that Fire is only described as "hot" or "dry" <note>Fire is a manifestation of the qualities, not the quality itself</note>; Heat is never described as "fire," nor is it a compound. Another reason is that every compound is either composed of its primary elements or is a 
<margin>6</margin> compound that has always existed. Thus, Heat exists before Fire, Moisture before Air, Cold before Water, and Dryness before Earth. However, this is understood by way of analysis <note>logical decomposition into constituent parts</note>. The same applies to the liver, the spleen, the gallbladder, the heart, the lungs, the head, the feet, the hands, 
<margin>9</margin> and all other remaining parts. Heat, as previously mentioned, arises from the constant motion of the [celestial] sphere, while Cold comes from the direction of the Center—meaning the **Earth**—which is called the center of the sphere of the universe. For this reason, it is the **Matter** <note>original: "al-hayula," from the Greek "hyle"</note> in which the benefit of all existence lies. Cold contradicts Heat in all its states— 
<margin>11</margin> meaning in its nature, motion, and stillness. Just as Heat is a quality that gathers similar things and separates opposing things, the same is true for the definition of Cold: it gathers opposing things and separates similar things. This occurs so that both difference and correspondence may occur 
<margin>15</margin> equally among the essences of opposites; otherwise, the part would be corrupted. <note>A Latin variant notes: "And thus it must be in all those things which are opposed to their qualities; if their disposition is not thus, it is injured and condemned."</note>

Therefore, O observer, you must investigate and look into these arduous and difficult-to-comprehend sciences to reach your goal. I have only provided you with these wondrous insights from the other sciences so that you may purify your soul and search earnestly for these marvelous secrets, so that you may attain what the 
<margin>18</margin> first Sages <note>the ancient Greek and Eastern philosophers</note> attained and ascend where they ascended.

# Chapter (10) on Stones

Among these are: **"Saturn"**, to which belong the stones: iron, diamond <note>original: "al-mas"; also refers to adamant</note>, antimony, onyx, and jet 
<margin>3</margin> (the clear black variety), turquoise, and magnet <note>lodestone</note>, and magnesia. It shares an affinity with gold, red ruby, golden marcasite, and hematite.

**"Jupiter"** has the stones: lead <note>original: "al-anak"</note>, and white and yellow ruby. It shares 
<margin>6</margin> an affinity with carnelian, gold, peridot <note>original: "zabaryad"</note>, rock crystal <note>original: "al-maha"</note>, and crystal; it governs every bright, white-colored stone.

**"Mars"** has the stones: red copper, the "cat-eye" stone <note>original: "al-sunnuri"</note>, and sulfur of all kinds. It shares an affinity with marcasite, bloodstone <note>original: "hajar al-dam"</note>, magnet, glass, carnelian, 
<margin>9</margin> and onyx; it governs every red stone that has a dark or dusky hue.

**"The Sun"** has the stones: gold, arsenic, garnet <note>original: "al-bijadi"</note>, diamond, "Pharaonic" glass, red shell, and every bright stone. It shares an affinity with hematite, 
<margin>12</margin> emery <note>original: "al-sunabadhaj"</note>, and red ruby.

**"Venus"** has the stones: red copper, lapis lazuli, pearls, shell, malachite <note>original: "al-dahnaj"</note>, and coral. It shares an affinity with silver, rock crystal <note>original: "al-maha"</note>, glass, and magnesia.

<margin>15</margin> **"Mercury"** has the stones: "hydrargyros" <note>original: "idramus," from the Greek for quicksilver/mercury</note>, "sabadhaj" <note>an unidentified stone, possibly a corruption of a Greek term</note>, emerald, and quicksilver. It shares an affinity with peridot, tin, glass, and marble.

These are their forms as mentioned by the authorities; according to them, these images possess specific effects. I am relaying to you the text of some of what they have mentioned.

# Images in Stones

Regarding the engravings of the images of the **Sun**: it is mentioned that whoever carves the "Greater Luminary" <note>original: "al-Nayyir al-A'zam," referring to the Sun</note> into a bezel of red ruby of pure redness, in the form of a king sitting upon a throne with a crown upon his head, a raven before him, and these letters beneath his feet: ☉ <term>Ah Qahir</term> <note>original: "اه قهر," likely meaning "O, Subduer," a name of power</note>—the one who carries this bezel will overcome all other kings. This is found in the *Book of the Interpretation of Spiritual Talismans translated by Baqratis* <note>original: "Baqrāṭīs," likely a medieval Arabic corruption of a Greek name like Hippocrates or Pancratius</note>, and he claimed that this should be done when the Sun is in its exaltation <note>The Sun's exaltation is in the sign of Aries</note>.

Among its engravings is what **Aristotle** mentioned to **Alexander**: whoever engraves the image of a lion upon a ruby stone with this mark Δ, while the rising sign is Leo and the Sun is within it, and the malefic planets <note>specifically Saturn and Mars</note> are absent from it—no one shall overcome him, his affairs shall be made easy for him, he shall succeed in everything he attempts, and he shall not see terrifying dreams in his sleep.

Among its engravings: whoever engraves on a diamond the image of a woman sitting on a chariot pulled by four horses, with a mirror in her right hand and a whip in her left, with seven rays upon her head and a pond within the bezel—this being done during its exaltation—this engraving on this stone produces awe and prestige for its wearer in the eyes of everyone he meets or deals with.

Among its engravings: whoever engraves this mark for the Sun on a bloodstone <term>Shadhana</term> <note>likely hematite or bloodstone, often used in talismans for health</note> during the first face <note>original: "al-wajh al-awwal," meaning the first decan (10 degrees) of a sign</note> of Leo, then the harm of epilepsy—which seizes one during the phase of the "Lesser Luminary" <note>original: "al-Nayyir al-Asghar," referring to the Moon</note>—shall depart from the wearer. This is the mark: ☉ ع ٩٦٥ ع.

Among its engravings is what **Hermes** mentioned in the *Book of al-Haditos*: he said that whoever engraves on a stone called *Samalinon* <note>A transliterated name, possibly from Greek; described as yellow with black spots and green "eyes," light and lustrous</note> the image of a fly during the hour of the Sun and its rising—then its wearer shall not be harmed by fire even if he enters it. He claimed this stone is found in the land of Persia.

Among its engravings for repelling snakes: whoever engraves on the bezel of a stone the image of a snake during the hour of the Sun, while it is at seven degrees of Aquarius, Saturn is at seven degrees of Aries, the Moon is at seven degrees of Scorpio, Jupiter is at two degrees of Sagittarius, and the Dragon's Tail <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> is at ten degrees of Sagittarius, and on its back are these symbols: د ل ا ح ۲ ۲ ح ۲ ۲ ٤ ٨ ٥ ☉ and around it are these symbols: ح ٤ ٢ ٦ ٧. If this stone is set in a gold ring and worn, no serpent, python, or viper will remain in the place where he is.

Among its engravings for repelling beetles: carve the image of a beetle on an agate bezel during the hour of the Sun while it is in its exaltation, with Saturn at seventeen degrees of Aquarius, Mercury at twenty-eight degrees of Gemini, the Moon at two degrees of Cancer, and Mars at the last degree of Libra. For him <note>Mercury</note>, there is engraved upon a stone known as the <term>Mantas</term> stone <note>original: "hajar Mantas." Footnotes suggest this may be Magnetite or a specific stone mentioned in the Latin tradition as "Magnatus"</note> the image of a man sitting upon a vaulted throne <note>original: "kursi muqarnas," referring to the decorative honeycomb-like architecture common in Islamic design</note>. In his right hand is a pen, and in the other is a scroll <term>tumar</term> upon which he is writing. This is done during his hour and exaltation.
<margin>3</margin> If the person carrying this gemstone is a member of the scribal profession, and he becomes weary of a ruler, the ruler will employ him, trust him with his affairs, and love him under all circumstances.

# The Moon

# Saturn

When a <term>bezoar stone</term> <note>original: "hajar baezahr," a stone-like mass found in animal guts, believed to have magical properties</note> is engraved during the <term>hour of Saturn</term> <note>In planetary magic, each hour of the day is ruled by a specific planet</note> while it is in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> at twenty-one <margin>3</margin> degrees of Libra, with the image of a man with a broad forehead and a long, frowning face, riding a shrine with two bulls before him. He is one who hopes for mercy, and around his neck is a necklace containing a human head and a fox head. This image has a powerful effect on preserving farms, cattle, crops, and plantations, and provides strength <margin>6</margin> for their upkeep. It is likewise effective for wells, the flow of rivers, the stability of buildings, resisting those who begin hostilities, settling grudges, and dispelling worries. It also prevents the wearer from fearing other people.

For Saturn, there is also engraved upon a diamond during his hour and rising this script: <margin>9</margin> <image-desc>Occult characters resembling a crescent, a right bracket, a cross, a script L, another bracket, a cross, and a crescent.</image-desc> This should be impressed into pitch to cast enmity and discord between people who love one another, and it is to be hidden in their location. The first seal should be kept safe; the maker must not touch it or go near it except at the time of making the impression.

For Saturn, there is also engraved upon a turquoise stone during his hour and rising the image of a man standing upon a chair <margin>12</margin> resembling a pulpit. Upon his head is something like a wound turban, and in his hand is a sickle. The effect resulting from this is the lengthening of the wearer’s life and the preservation of his vitality.

For Saturn, when there is engraved upon a yellow <term>amber</term> <note>original: "kahraba"</note> gemstone the image of a wolf during his hour, with the Rising Sign being Capricorn, <margin>15</margin> while Saturn is in Leo at twenty-three degrees, Mercury is in Virgo at two degrees, and Mars is in nineteen degrees of Libra—and this script is drawn around it: <margin>18</margin> <image-desc>A sequence of planetary/occult characters: a 'V', a triangle, two crosses, an epsilon, a cross, a crescent, a 'D', and an 'X'.</image-desc> If it is set in a silver ring and worn, then flies will flee

<column-break/>

from the place of the wearer; they will not attack him or anyone else, nor will they appear in his place at all, nor enter any land where he is present by any means.

For Saturn, to repel locusts, engrave on an obsidian stone the image of a locust during his hour and rising, while he is <margin>3</margin> at two degrees of Aries, Mars is at five degrees of Cancer, and the Moon is at three degrees of Capricorn. At these degrees, the talisman takes effect. Draw around the locust this script: <image-desc>Four occult characters: a stylized E, an epsilon, a number 1, and a phi-like symbol.</image-desc> Place beneath it the skin of a rabbit after it is assembled; then no locusts will ever enter the place where <margin>6</margin> the talisman is kept, whether it is alone or with the person carrying it.

For Saturn, engrave on any of his stones that you wish the image of a rabbit, with the Rising Sign in Libra, Saturn at thirteen degrees of Gemini, and the Sun at five degrees of <margin>9</margin> Cancer. Draw around it this script: <image-desc>A line of complex occult symbols and numerals including 7, 4, 8, and cursive shapes.</image-desc> Then set it in a ring and wear it; the woman with whom the wearer has intercourse will not conceive from him as long as it is with him.

# Jupiter

<margin>12</margin> Engrave for him on a white sapphire gemstone the image of a man with a crown on his head, sitting upon a throne that has four legs. Each leg of the throne rests upon the neck of a standing man, and these men have wings. The seated man has his hand raised in prayer. This is done during Jupiter's hour while he is in his <term>exaltation</term> <note>The sign where a planet's influence is most harmonious and powerful</note>. The effect of this ring for its wearer is to increase his prestige <margin>15</margin> and status, to acquire wealth, to reunite family and loved ones, to increase the number of children and preserve them, to settle matters in the best possible way, and to bring to completion the righteous deeds the wearer begins.

### Mars

For Mars, the image of a man riding a lion is engraved upon a <term>magnetite stone</term> <note>original: "hajar maghnitis," a naturally magnetized piece of the mineral magnetite, traditionally used in navigation and magic</note>. In his right hand is a drawn sword and in his left hand is a human head. This is done during the <term>hour of Mars</term> <note>The specific hour of the day governed by the planet Mars</note> while it is in the second <term>face</term> <note>A "face" or "decan" is a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Aries <gloss>3</gloss>. This talisman performs wondrous deeds in both evil and good, though its actions in evil are more frequent.

Another engraving for Mars involves carving onto one of the stones associated with the planet the image of a standing man wearing armor and girded with <gloss>6</gloss> two swords: one drawn in his right hand and a human head in his left hand, performed during his hour. When the wearer has this image, he should expect to possess <gloss>6</gloss> <term>awe and dominance</term> <note>original: "al-mahaba wa-l-satwa," reflecting the martial power of the planet</note> over everyone who sees him or associates with him. I have seen this exact image on a <term>carnelian</term> <note>original: "aqiq," a reddish-brown semi-precious stone</note> gemstone belonging to a practitioner of this craft <gloss>9</gloss>.

Also for Mars, when the image of a lion is engraved on an <term>onyx stone</term> <note>original: "hajar al-jaz'," often associated in medieval lapidaries with sadness or protection, depending on the context</note> with this script <insert>H 811 M</insert> <gloss>9</gloss> placed before it, during his hour and the <term>ascendant</term> of his house, then if anyone with <gloss>12</gloss> flowing blood from any of their limbs holds this stone, it will stop the bleeding immediately and prevent it from flowing. Know this well.

Talismans are also made for these planets that have wondrous effects according to limited proportions. <gloss>12</gloss> Among them is a talisman for the Sun, made during its hour and the first face of Leo, which removes the symptoms of the <term>wicked soul</term> <note>likely referring to depression, anxiety, or spiritual oppression</note> and settles pains of the liver and stomach, as well as difficult illnesses.

It repels the plots of enemies, and the wearer succeeds in his travels and remains safe from the assassination of his foe.

For the Sun also, one should engrave on a <term>green sapphire</term> <note>original: "yaqut akhdar," though 'yaqut' often means ruby, green 'yaqut' usually refers to sapphire or occasionally emerald</note> the image of a man with the face of a lion and the feet of <gloss>3</gloss> a bird. Beneath his feet is a dragon with a head, and in his right hand is a javelin with which he stabs the head of the dragon. This is done during the Sun's hour and the first face of its <term>house of exaltation</term> <note>The sign where a planet's influence is most potent; for the Sun, this is Aries</note>. Its effect is to remove <gloss>6</gloss> enemies for its wearer and grant him awe and fear in their hearts.

Also for the Sun, one may engrave on a <term>crystal stone</term> <note>original: "hajar billur," likely rock crystal</note> the image of a handsome man wearing a cap, riding an eagle. Its effect <gloss>6</gloss> is to make you beloved by judges and the masters of religious laws. The engraving should be during the Sun's hour and its exaltation.

For the Sun, one may also engrave upon the stone known as the <term>facilitator of birth</term> <note>original: "musahel al-wilada," also known as the Aetites or 'Eagle Stone,' a geode believed to assist in labor</note> the image of an eagle, during the Sun's hour <gloss>9</gloss> and the rising of the first face of Sagittarius. If the wearer of this image goes out to a place of birds and intends to catch them, they will gather around him in great numbers and not leave him. The one who holds it will also be accepted and beloved among people.

This stone is one that tends toward redness; in its core is a stone that moves if shaken, and if <gloss>12</gloss> it is rubbed, a white liquid comes out of it. Its unique property is that if a woman hangs it upon herself, she will never become pregnant.

**Hermes** mentioned that this stone is blessed among stones. Whoever takes it and engraves <gloss>15</gloss> upon it the image of a fox on the day of **Jupiter** during his hour, with the Moon looking toward him and Jupiter in Pisces, its effect is such that if a human keeps it with him, both Jinn and humans will fear him.

For Jupiter also, if the image of a nightingale is engraved on this stone during the hour of Jupiter while he is in his <gloss>18</gloss> house of exaltation, and this stone is washed and someone is given the water to drink, he will see the <term>spiritual beings</term> <note>original: "al-arwah al-ruhaniyya," referring to angels or spirits</note> and may employ them in whatever he wishes. This was also mentioned by **Hermes**, and it contains what it contains of signs and hints.

...from it, and there is no dispensing with it for the student and the researcher of this matter. So let your gaze, O observer, be for your own sake. Whenever any part of this art becomes clear to you, do not reveal it to anyone else. Know that the <margin>3</margin> people who find the most pleasure in the sciences are those who do not resort to making a living from them, but rather occupy themselves with them and study them to become part of the elite and distinguish themselves from the common folk. Many in the world, not knowing the difficulty of the aims of <margin>6</margin> this science, task the astrologer <note>original: "al-munajjim"</note> at times with things that are not even within the power of the celestial spheres <note>original: "al-falak," the rotating shells that medieval science believed carried the planets</note>, let alone within the power of the astrologer. If he succeeds, they do not praise him for his success, and if he errs, his worth diminishes in their eyes. Therefore, you must not <margin>9</margin> violate this secret for the common people. Indeed, the sages only grasped these spiritual sciences through great hardship and toil. They reached what they reached through diligence, extensive research, and excellence of the intellect. For through the excellence of the intellect, one gains the power to coincide with the correct judgment in matters where <margin>12</margin> conflicting opinions clash, and the strength to verify it. It is the excellence of deducing what is correct among opinions, and this is a type of discernment. In short, it is the clarity of the rational soul <note>original: "al-nafs al-natiqa," the part of the soul responsible for reason in Aristotelian philosophy</note> and the granting of power to the imaginative faculty along with the clarity of its pathways and its speed in accepting what it desires, combined with the quick <margin>15</margin> response of the required sage. The intellect is a potent actor, while the judgment is a weak recipient. An example of the potent and the weak is that the potent acts with difficulty while the weak is acted upon with ease. Just as "acuteness" <note>original: "dhaka’," which means both intelligence and the intensity of light or fire</note> is the excellence of sensing a thing quickly without time, or in a time that is not delayed, it is <margin>18</margin> an apprehension by the mind through swift investigation. Likewise, the excellence of sense-perception is the acceptance of the desired thing without time. It is derived from the "acuteness of fire," in that it acts quickly, and the "acuteness of the sun," which penetrates the air quickly and illuminates it in its place due to its thinness and clarity. Likewise, the intelligent person shines by his clarity.

For the Moon, in its hour and the first face <note>A "face" or "decan" is a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Cancer, there is a talisman for the growth of crops and trees and all <margin>3</margin> types of plants.

For Saturn, in its hour and the third face of Aquarius, there is a talisman that cures urinary incontinence and stops <margin>6</margin> hemorrhaging in women.

For Jupiter, in its hour while it is in the second face of Sagittarius and the Sun is joined to it, there is a talisman that stops excessive rain that threatens flooding.

<margin>9</margin> For Mars, in its hour while it is in the first face of Scorpio, there is a talisman that emboldens the coward, breaks the anger of the ruler, and repels the harm of thieves, predatory beasts, wolves, and every evil thing.

For Venus, in its hour while she is in the first face of Pisces, there is a talisman that heals women <margin>12</margin> of uterine ailments, cures the wicked soul afflicted by melancholy <note>original: "al-mali-khuliya"</note>, gladdens the heart, and aids in increasing libido <note>original: "al-bah"</note>. In the first face of Taurus, there is a talisman that inspires love and performs grand deeds.

For Mercury, in his hour while he is in the first face of Gemini, there is a talisman that sharpens the intellect <margin>15</margin>, improves thought, encourages the pursuit of sciences, and is used to gain prestige among people and similar things.

...and its delicacy, so it permeates the sought-after object and senses it quickly, perceiving it through its encompassing of the dead or the living, in whatever way it is possible to perceive the required judgment. So know that.

Let us return to where we were. We say also that for every zodiac sign <term>Zodiac sign: one of the twelve 30-degree segments of the celestial belt</term> there are three faces <term>Faces: also known as decans, these are 10-degree subdivisions of a sign, each ruled by a different planet</term>. In <margin>3</margin> each of these faces are the images, statues, and likenesses described by the sages. This is but a part of the whole. These faces are divided among the planets according to their succession in their celestial spheres. When <margin>6</margin> the division reaches the lowest planet <note>The Moon</note>, it returns and goes back to the highest, most elevated planet <note>Saturn</note>. They have natures and forms that correspond to the natures and forms of their planetary lords. Because of <margin>9</margin> this, they match them in what they indicate regarding their essence, whether in agreement or disagreement of actions.

(Among these is the **first face of Aries**. According to the head of <margin>10</margin> this craft <note>Likely referring to the astrologer Abu Ma'shar</note>, there rises in it an angry man, black-skinned with red eyes, holding an axe. He has tied a white cloth around his waist. He is large in body and great in his own estimation. This face belongs to **Mars**. It is a face of <margin>12</margin> ferocity, power, loftiness, and impudence. It is complete and abundant in its essence, nature, and instinct.)

There rises in the **second face of Aries** a woman wearing a green garment who has only one leg <margin>14</margin>. This face belongs to **Venus**. Its action is femininity, delicacy, cleanliness, kindness, amusement, <margin>15</margin> joy, and decoration.

And in its third face <note>This refers to the third decan of Taurus, continuing the sequence from the previous section.</note> there rises a man of evil and cunning, and before him is a woman who has donned a veil, holding a bird in her hand. This face belongs to **Mars** <note>original: "al-Marrikh"</note>; it is a face of marriage, embracing, desire, coitus,
<margin>3</margin> lust, and the love of ease and comfort.

Know, O observer, that within the images of these faces lies a secret known only to the experienced sage who is insightful in extracting obscure matters. This is because a planet counteracts <note>literally "breaks"</note> another planet, the **term** <term>hadd: a five-fold subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> 
<margin>6</margin> counteracts the face, the face counteracts the house <note>the zodiac sign itself</note>, and the temperaments overlap one another—just like water
which extinguishes the heat of fire, fire which removes the coldness of water, water which moistens the dryness of
the earth, and the earth which dries the moisture of water. When these temperaments multiply and compete,
<margin>9</margin> the strongest and most abundant among them prevails. Yet, when they are equal and balanced, their powers, 
effects, and works become moderate and equal. Know that the Sun is strengthened by the nature of Mars, and Mars is strengthened by the nature of 
the Sun. Know also that excess in the temperaments corrupts them and diminishes their integrity and perfection.
<margin>12</margin> After perfect health comes sickness, and at the completion of the fruit comes the harvest. A great substance 
opposes a weak one through its weight and strength, yet the small acts upon the great through its subtlety and refinement—much like the snake
which kills the largest of beasts. Likewise, powerful serpents are killed by the tiny, lowly ant
<margin>15</margin> through sheer numbers, despite the ant's smallness and fragility. Therefore, understand these signs. The method used by the sages regarding these
faces is to know what corresponds to the planet and what corresponds to the sign of the face in terms of magical works. 
Then, you should draw the mentioned images upon the materials <note>metals or stones</note> that correspond to that planet while it is in that
<margin>18</margin> face. This will bring the mentioned effects into manifestation and produce them in the "world of generation and corruption" <note>the physical, sublunary world</note>.
If it is possible, in addition to this, for the Sun to be rising in the hour of that planet or 
be in aspect with it, the matter will be even more effective. But avoid what we have mentioned regarding the Sun being with a planet that overpowers
<margin>21</margin> that specific nature.

### Chapter (12)

As for a group among the people of India, the foundation of their works regarding talismans relies upon 
<margin>3</margin> the **decanates** <term>Drijanat: derived from the Sanskrit 'drekkana,' these are ten-degree subdivisions of a sign</term>. This is because every rising sign is divided into three equal parts, each part being ten degrees. 
Each part is called a **decan** <note>original: "Drijan"</note> and is attributed to one of the seven planets, which is then called the Lord of 
the Decan. The first part of the rising sign is assigned to the Lord of the Sign, the 
<margin>6</margin> second part to the Lord of the fifth house, and the third part to the Lord of the ninth house. These three—the rising sign, the fifth, and the ninth—always 
form a single **triplicity** <note>a group of three signs of the same element</note>.

The first decan of **Aries** <note>original: "al-Hamal"</note> belongs to **Mars**. In it, one creates talismans for wars, 
<margin>9</margin> so that their possessor may be a victor and never vanquished. In this decan, one can also curdle sheep’s milk or spoil its butter and fat.

The second decan of Aries belongs to **the Sun**. In it, one crafts talismans for princes 
and sultans to gain their favor and ward off their harm.
<margin>12</margin> The third decan of Aries belongs to **Jupiter** <note>original: "al-Mushtari"</note>. In it, one crafts talismans for dealing with 
judges and jurists, reconciling them, and unifying their word if they have been divided.

The first decan of **Taurus** <note>original: "al-Thawr"</note> belongs to **Venus** <note>original: "al-Zahra"</note>. In it, one crafts talismans for reconciliation 
<margin>15</margin> between men and women.

The second decan of Taurus belongs to **Mercury** <note>original: "Utarid"</note>. In it, one crafts talismans of enmity, the binding of 
lusts <note>spells for impotence or sexual restraint</note>, and the instigation of evil specifically among women.

The first **drekkana** <term>drekkana: a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as a 'face', derived from Sanskrit</term> of **Virgo** <note>original: "al-Sunbulah", literally "The Ear of Corn"</note> belongs to **Mercury**. <margin>3</margin> The second **drekkana** of it belongs to **Saturn**. In it, a talisman is made to cause the corruption of the state of scribes.

<margin>6</margin> The first **drekkana** of **Libra** <note>original: "al-Mizan", "The Scales"</note> belongs to **Venus**. In it, talismans for agitation <note>likely erotic arousal or excitement</note>,

<margin>18</margin> and intimacy are made.
The second **drekkana** of it belongs to **Mars**. In it, talismans of agitation and the tearing of veils <note>meaning the exposure of secrets or public scandal</note> are made.

So, these are the **drekkana** <term>drekkana: a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as a 'face', used to refine astrological predictions and magic</term> which are the mainstay of their works. They claim, moreover, that the foundation and the mainstay for the completion of all their works can only be achieved through sincerity of thought and correctness of intention. Their leader claimed that the attraction 
<margin>3</margin> of the powers of the planets is only achieved through sincerity of thought; for the higher powers are the forms of the lower powers, and the lower forms are like their materials. They are connected to one another, attracting each other, because their physical 
<margin>5</margin> essence is a single essence, and their spiritual essence is also a single essence.
<margin>6</margin> A group of their **Brahmins** <note>original: "barahimatihim", referring to the priestly class of India, often cited in medieval Arabic texts as sources of ancient wisdom</note> claimed that these powers are subtle graces created by the Creator within His creation, making them 
<margin>7</margin> lessons for them and a mercy among them. In this regard, they created infinite circles that point to the reality of thought, its ultimate end, and its correctness. When they wished to join the ranks of the **Great Lawgivers** 
<margin>9</margin> and become statesmen and those called "holy," reaching for the heights, they would discipline their souls and 
<margin>10</margin> purify themselves of all impurities. They would begin this work of sanctification during the first hour of 
<margin>11</margin> Sunday—which is the hour and the day of the Sun—then they would fast for forty days. During these 
<margin>12</margin> days, they would avoid meat and sustain themselves on what the earth produces of plants, herbs, and grains, because 
<margin>13</margin> they do not believe in the destruction of any animal. They would wash themselves every day during the hours of the Sun and the Moon. 
<margin>14</margin> Some of them would wash seven times a day during the hours of the planets, monitoring the entry of 
<margin>15</margin> the hours and washing at their beginnings. They would commit to starting this work at times when 
<margin>16</margin> the planets were auspicious. If their purification coincided with the auspiciousness of the Sun and Moon and 
<margin>17</margin> their safety from malevolent influences, then "bravo, bravo!" <note>original: "bakh bakh", an Arabic expression of high praise or excellence</note>—that matter was considered by them to be an increase in holiness. And yet...

For this reason, they reduce their food every day until their meal on the last day is only one-quarter of a tenth <note>i.e., one-fortieth (1/40th)</note> of what they ate on the first day. During this time and upon completing the fast, they employ medicines they have become accustomed to 
<margin>3</margin> preparing, so that they might be protected by taking them in place of food and drink, no longer requiring sustenance. When they do this, 
they find within themselves signs of intelligence and a capacity to memorize whatever they wish to preserve and understand. Their insight sharpens, 
their mind becomes keen, the "earthliness" <note>referring to heavy, material impulses</note> within them diminishes, heaviness departs, and a sense of lightness prevails. A longing appears 
<margin>6</margin> to ascend to the **World of Light** <note>original: " عالم النور" (ʿālam al-nūr), a common Gnostic and Neoplatonic concept referring to the divine realm of pure spirit</note>, and the soul turns away from worldly desires and obscene pleasures. It is then 
that they become capable of attracting the celestial powers; they perform wonders, achieve their goals, 
and come to know the cosmic cycles and the realities of their existence within them—what has been decreed for them and what remains for them. This 
<margin>9</margin> is the **Origin of Light**. Their proof for this is what they found recorded in the beginning of the **Scripture of the Budd** <term>Budd: in medieval Arabic texts, this term refers to the Buddha or a specific idol/sage associated with Indian or Sabian wisdom</term>, which 
is their "secret of secrets" which they reveal to no one. The opening of the scripture begins by placing at its start 
the figures of the numbers representing the movements of the celestial spheres, composed of the lights of those souls devoted to the worship of the **Highest Light**. 
<margin>12</margin> For this, they created symbols based on the **four simple natures** <note>the classical elements: heat, cold, moisture, and dryness</note>, from which nothing is diminished 
so long as the movements of the spheres remain connected to the world. For this reason, the **Budd** was a messenger to them, for whom the Light 
hastens its rays which are connected to the lower powers. This occurs in the presence of the **Highest Light**, through which 
<margin>14</margin> the completion of all things is achieved. At that point, they come to know the nature of the **Temperament** <note>original: "al-mizāj", referring to the balance of the four humors/natures</note>, and they can envision whatever forms they desire. 
They established all the **Divine Laws** <note>original: "nawāmīs", often referring to revealed or natural laws governing the cosmos</note>, and the spirits of the planets obeyed them. In this book, 
they also possess secrets by which they know the true realities of things. Despite this, they recognize the **Creator** 
<margin>18</margin> and know that He is the **Cause of All**, and they treat the things they do as a means and a ladder 

<column-break/>

<page-num>١٣٩</page-num>

to reach Him and unite with His light. We have mentioned this as a reminder of their foundations, the origins of their practices, and what 
the followers of their laws hold fast to. This is the literal text of this man's words.
<margin>3</margin> They also possess wondrous things that, were I to include them, would make this book too long. Among these is **The Head** which 
the priests of a certain group among them believe in. This is because they set it up facing the "Head of the Dragon" <note>a lunar node in astrology</note>. They 
seek out a man who is brown-skinned and blue-eyed with a reddish-gray tint, having joined eyebrows and thick hair. They trick 
<margin>6</margin> him with things he desires until they secure him in the house of the temples. He is stripped naked and then seated in a stone jar that has been filled 
with sesame oil up to his throat. A lid is fitted over him at his head, with just enough space for his head to emerge. 
They nail the lid down and seal it with lead, so his head remains outside while his body is submerged in the oil. 
<margin>9</margin> Then they feed him dried figs soaked in sesame oil every day in a specific amount. 
They burn incense near his nose and face—an incense they call the **Incense of Amazement** <note>original: "bukhur al-bahata", likely a hallucinogenic or stupefying substance</note>—and they speak to him in their private tongue. 
They continue this for forty days, giving him no water to drink. What he produces <note>i.e., bodily waste</note> remains in that 
<margin>12</margin> oil until his nerves soften, his joints loosen, and his veins swell, until from his softness he becomes like wax. 
Then a day is prepared for him when they gather together, speaking their words and burning incense. 
They take hold of his head and pull it from the first vertebra; it stretches with them, the veins still attached, until 
<margin>15</margin> they all come out from the vertebra, and the entire body remains in the oil. Then they place the head in a niche upon 
sifted ash, which they make from the ash of olives mixed with a little ash from the burnt remains of bodies. 
They surround it with embroidered cotton and burn their incense for it. Then that **Head** informs them 
<margin>18</margin> of matters such as high and low prices, the downfall of dynasties, and what will occur in the world; and it continues...
