...the head's eyes remain open, though they do not blink. Occasionally, the practitioners might neglect the rites of the planets, so the head demands these of them, rebukes them for certain things, and informs them of what will befall them personally. They might also ask it about sciences <margin>3</margin> and crafts, and it answers them. Then, they remove the rest of its body from the basin and extract its liver, dissecting it to find signs of what they require. Similarly, they use the shoulder bones and the joints to divine what they need. They do not shave their hair, <margin>6</margin> nor do they eat or drink except in the head's name. They were exposed during the days of al-Muqtadir <note>Al-Muqtadir was the Abbasid Caliph who reigned from 908 to 932 CE. This passage reflects the historical tension between the central Islamic government and the pagan/Hermetic community of Harran.</note>, who ordered that one of their temples be entered. The head was found there after they were expelled from the temple, and he ordered its burial.

A group among them assigned colors to the planetary spheres, using symbols based on <margin>9</margin> the nature of the materials that receive these influences. They said that the sphere of Saturn is a dusty red, like the color of a ruby; the sphere of Jupiter is a dusty white; the sphere of Mars is yellow, green, and red, like the color of red gold; <margin>12</margin> the sphere of the Sun is a dusty gilded color; the sphere of Venus is a gilded red; the sphere of Mercury is a mixture of all colors; and the sphere of the Moon is green, white, and spotted.

They assigned "faces" <note>The "faces" or decans are 10-degree subdivisions of the zodiac signs, here used as specific windows of planetary power.</note> to the planets which indicate the nature of the work to be performed, and they created talismans for these faces to exert influence. They gave each planet three faces, and for each face, two talismans. <margin>15</margin> Furthermore, they assigned colors to these faces: they said that the **red** faces are suitable for grand affairs, for every matter of authority, and for any talisman made for one seeking aid. The **black** face is <margin>18</margin> for diseases, reliance, causing death, and all manner of afflictions and their like. The **white** face represents radiance, light, and joy; it is suitable for all talismans of good, such as intimacy, love, and the like. The **yellow** face is for attracting or repelling non-speaking animals <note>i.e., livestock or wild beasts</note>, and also for works of evil.

From the first [face] of **Mercury**, a <term>talisman (طلسم)</term> is fashioned so that a beard shall never grow on anyone’s face. From the second [face] of it, a talisman is fashioned to draw rivers to any place you desire.

<margin>3</margin> From the first face of the **Moon**, two talismans are fashioned: the first to attract any of the princes or leaders you wish; the second is to harmonize the hearts of kings to love whomever you desire, so that they cannot endure being away from him or meeting with him. From the second face, [from] the first [part] of it, a talisman is fashioned <margin>6</margin> for the <term>binding (ʿaqd)</term> <note>A ritual meant to cause impotence or "tie" a person's capability.</note> of any man you wish so that he cannot have intimacy with a woman. From the second part of the second face, a talisman is fashioned to release anyone whose desire for women has been "bound." From the third face of the **Moon**, from the first [part] of it, a talisman is fashioned to disperse people from their lands and exile them from <margin>9</margin> their homelands. From the second part of the third face, a talisman is made so that no harmful predator shall stay in any place you wish.

These are the judgments for the talismans of the planets according to their placements.

I have seen a treatise on the craft of talismans by **Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi**, <margin>12</margin> the philosopher of the Arabs. His standing in observation and philosophy is well known. I have included what I found of it in my book titled *The History of the Philosophers of the Arabs*. I mentioned this treatise of his there among the wonders he composed. In this treatise, he recorded certain [astrological] proportions which he claimed to have tested. <margin>15</margin> Among them is his saying: "One should seek for the fashioning of talismans for sympathy, love, and affection that the **Moon** be in **Taurus** and connected to **Venus** in the sign of **Pisces**, or that the **Moon** be in the sign of **Pisces**..."

Talismans for <margin>12</margin> **scribes, ministers, and governors** are made when the **Moon** is connected to **Mercury**, with **Mercury** in the sign of **Gemini** or **Virgo**, and the **Moon** is at full light (Full Moon).

Know that the square aspect of the **Moon** may reveal the nature of every planet, provided that <margin>15</margin> it is in one of the <term>Angles (awtad)</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of an astrological chart.</note>, the strongest of which is the tenth [the Midheaven]. This applies to auspicious works with the **Benefics** <note>Usually Jupiter and Venus.</note>. As for inauspicious works, it is discouraged, except with the **Malefics** <note>Usually Saturn and Mars.</note> when the intent is to ruin something or bring misfortune. **Saturn** and **Mars** are the guarantors of that, being the strongest factors aiding that type of work along with the form of the [astrological] proportion.

Know that the Moon’s <term>application (iṭṭiṣāl)</term> <note>In astrology, an "application" occurs when a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one.</note> to the planets while it is ahead of the Sun is stronger than its application when it is behind the Sun. Its application to the Sun from a <term>trine (tathlīth)</term> or <term>sextile (tasdīs)</term> <note>A "trine" is an angle of 120 degrees and a "sextile" is 60 degrees; both are considered highly favorable alignments.</note> is utilized for every lofty matter,
<margin>3</margin> such as seeking kingship, leadership, victory, or prominence. Its presence in the <term>tenth house</term> <note>The "tenth house" represents career, status, and authority.</note> is more effective and better than in the fourth or seventh. There is no good to be found in its <term>waning (maḥāq)</term> or its <term>combustion (iḥtirāq)</term>. <note>Combustion occurs when a planet is so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up" or hidden.</note> Similarly, its application to **Venus** from a trine, sextile, square, or opposition is good, but it is not like **Jupiter**; rather, Jupiter is
<margin>6</margin> more effective in that regard. Venus is more effective in matters of women’s affection, sympathy, and enduring love, because that is in her nature—especially if the trine occurs in **Water** or **Earth** signs. Perform what you desire
with an <term>ascendant (ṭāliʿ)</term> in a Water or Earth sign. If the trine is from **Fire** or **Air** signs, then perform
<margin>9</margin> what you desire with a Fire or Air ascendant.

This man—I mean **al-Razi** <note>original: "al-Razi" - referring to the famous Persian polymath Rhazes (d. 925 AD).</note>—is one from whom knowledge should be taken, due to his extensive research and his investigation into the ancient sciences. However, the absolute master of this craft, who is
<margin>12</margin> the foremost authority in it, is **Abu Musa Jabir ibn Hayyan al-Sufi** <note>original: "Jabir ibn Hayyan" - known in the West as Geber, the legendary father of chemistry and alchemy.</note>—may God Almighty have mercy on him and grant us his knowledge. He is the author of the *Book of Research on the Craft of Talismans*, the author of the *Great Book of Talismans* which he organized into fifty treatises, and the author of the *Book of the Key to the
<margin>15</margin> Images of the Degrees and Their Astrological Effects*, and the author of the *Comprehensive Book on the Astrolabe, in Theory and Practice*, which contains over a thousand chapters. In it, he mentioned marvelous operations that no one before him had ever reached. And what would you think of his *Great Book of Talismans*, in which he collected
<margin>18</margin> the wonders of the sciences? For a long time, people have been stingy with these secrets and would not permit them to be mentioned—secrets regarding the science of talismans, images, occult properties, the actions of the planets, the actions of natures, and their influences. # The Third Treatise

In this treatise, I shall mention the shares of the planets within the <term>three generated beings</term> <note>original: "al-muwalladāt al-thalāth"; refers to the three kingdoms of nature: minerals, plants, and animals.</note> because in the world of <term>generation and corruption</term> <note>A philosophical term for the physical world where things are born, change, and decay.</note> there is nothing that accepts magical work except for them, as the <term>elements</term> <note>original: "al-ustuqussāt"; from the Greek "stoicheia."</note> are in a state of flux and do not receive impressions. <margin>3</margin> I will also discuss the blending of these elements with one another so that the desired magical works may be achieved through the influence of either elemental heat or natural heat. This influence is carried either by <term>incense</term> <note>original: "dukhna"</note> for fumigation, or by something intended to be ingested into the stomach as food or drink. Along with this, I will include whatever else is appropriate for this treatise. <margin>6</margin>

## Chapter (1)

We have already described to you, O observer, in the preceding treatise regarding the actions of talismans and images, their influences, their proportions, and their pairings, as much as we were able to bestow upon you. We noted that everything <margin>9</margin> formed in the belly of the earth, upon its surface, and in the air above and beyond it, has a form in the <term>celestial sphere</term> <note>original: "al-falak"</note> that resembles its own form, a shape that corresponds to it, and a counterpart that is its likeness. For whenever the Sun reaches a position in the sphere through its perpetual motion, it performs an action different from the one before it; thus its actions are diverse <margin>12</margin> and perpetual. This is due to the changing positions of the <term>wandering planets</term> <note>original: "al-kawākib al-mutahayyira"; the planets known to the ancients (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn).</note> and the fixed stars in their dwellings. Therefore, whenever there is a need to set something in motion...

<column-break/>

<page-num>148</page-num>

...[Jabir] called "The Synthesis" <note>original: "al-Tajmīʿ"; a famous work by Jabir ibn Hayyan regarding the artificial creation of life.</note> in which he mentioned the making of both rational and irrational animals. However, **Jabir** discussed it in that book from a natural perspective, aiming for works that resemble the work of Nature itself. As for the leader <margin>3</margin> **Plato**, he mentioned this through celestial works and spiritual images whose subjects are natural materials. Whoever wishes to understand what I have mentioned should examine those sources. We shall include in this book of ours, when we reach the appropriate place, as much of that as possible. Here is the conclusion of this <margin>6</margin> **Second Treatise**.

...one observes the proper time for it. When its form moves within the <term>celestial sphere</term> <note>original: "al-falak"</note> and aligns with the place where the action is intended to occur, we activate its nature by incorporating something terrestrial or aerial that resembles both natures. From this, a great spiritual movement occurs within the terrestrial object according to the intended purpose. For talismans act through two directions: one is celestial and the other is terrestrial. This is what I have deposited in this treatise regarding the types of magic related to the <term>science of talismans</term> <note>original: "ilm al-talsamāt"</note> in its high and noble status.

<margin>6</margin> ۞ The planets possess specific matters and unique properties regarding the magical works one attempts, which belong to them alone.

♄ ۞ **Saturn** ۞ is the fountainhead of the <term>retentive power</term> <note>original: "al-quwwa al-māsika"; one of the four natural faculties in medieval physiology, responsible for holding nutrients or qualities within an organ.</note>. To it belongs the oversight of the obscure celestial sciences, the seeking of the causes of things and the discovery of their ends, the speaking of wonders, and the knowledge of secrets and hidden <margin>9</margin> matters. Among languages, it claims Coptic and Hebrew. Of the limbs, it rules the right ear on the outside of the body, and on the inside, the spleen, from whose substance the power of the <term>black bile</term> <note>original: "al-khilt al-sawdāwī"; one of the four humors of Greco-Arabic medicine, associated with melancholy and Saturn.</note> humor grows throughout all parts of the body and its joints, and through which the cohesion of its parts is maintained. Of garments, it rules <margin>12</margin> every coarse cloth. Of crafts, it rules leather-working, agriculture, the extraction of minerals, and construction. Of tastes, it rules those that are harsh and astringent, like <term>myrobalan</term> <note>original: "al-ihlīlaj"; a fruit used in medieval medicine.</note>. Of places, it rules black mountains, dark valleys, tunnels, wells, graves, and deserts. Of gems, it rules onyx and <margin>15</margin> black stones and the magnet [loadstone]. Of metals, it rules lead and iron and everything that is black in color and foul in smell. Of plants, it rules the oak, <term>halfah grass</term> <note>original: "al-asf"</note>, carob, the palm tree, vines, boxthorn, cumin, rue, onion, and everything with thick leaves and every tree that has <margin>18</margin> painful thorns. Of drugs, it rules aloes, myrrh, and their likes, wild castor, and wild colocynth.

## Chapter (2)

### The signs of the Zodiac also have states specific to them:

**۞Aries۞** rules the head, the face, the pupils of the eyes, and the ears among the body parts. Among colors, it rules yellow and a moderate red <note>original: *croceum cum rubo mixtum* from the Latin Picatrix; a saffron-red blend</note>. Among tastes, it rules bitterness. Among places, it rules deserts, sites of fires, and the hideouts of thieves. Among minerals, it rules those worked by fire. Among animals, it rules all four-legged creatures with cloven hooves.
**۞Taurus۞** rules the neck, the Adam's apple, and the larynx among the body parts. Among colors, it rules a mixture of green and white. Among tastes, it rules sourness. Among places, it rules all inhabited lands, tilled soil, and gardens. Among plants, it rules tall trees whose fruit is eaten and which can survive without much water, as well as every tree with a pleasant taste and scent. Among animals, it rules all four-legged creatures with cloven hooves.
**۞Gemini۞** rules the two shoulders, the two upper arms, the two hands, and the two shoulder blades among the body parts. Among colors, it rules green tinged with yellow. Among tastes, it rules sweetness. Among places, it rules mountains <note>Manuscript variation: houses and places of prayer in high mountains</note>, hunting grounds, and tilled earth. Among plants, it rules tall trees. Among animals, it rules humans, monkeys, water birds, and every bird with an exquisite melody and beautiful song.
**۞Cancer۞** rules the chest, the breasts, the stomach, the spleen, the lungs, the ribs, and the hidden areas of the chest among the body parts. Among colors, it rules white and a smoky dust-color. Among tastes, it rules saltiness. Among places, it rules marshes, hills, thickets, coastlines, riverbanks, and wooded areas. Among gems, it rules water-gems <note>likely referring to pearls or crystals</note>.

...and the sciences of the affairs of the sick and their treatment, and the knowledge of narratives and reports. Among languages, it rules the tongue of the Slavs <note>original: *al-Saqaliba*; historically referring to Slavic peoples of Eastern Europe</note> and the Sabaeans <note>original: *al-Sabi'a*; a religious group from Harran known for star-worship and philosophy</note>. Among the body parts, it rules the left eye by day and the right eye by night for men, and for women the opposite. In the interior of the body, it rules the lungs, through which breathing occurs—sometimes by inhaling air from outside the body to preserve the innate heat <term>al-harara al-ghariziya</term> <note>the vital warmth that medieval physicians believed sustained life</note>, and sometimes by expelling it outward. Among religions, it rules the faith of the Sabaeans and Divine Revelation. Among garments, it rules furs and kerchiefs. Among the crafts, it rules weaving, couriers, farming, planting, irrigation, and navigation. Among tastes, it rules blandness. Among places, it rules springs, salt flats, snowy places, and all bodies of water. Among gems, it rules small pearls. Among minerals, it rules silver and "white bodies" <note>an alchemical term for silver-like alloys or purified metals</note>. Among plants, it rules papyrus, reeds, chamomile, and every sweet-smelling white plant, as well as every tree that does not stand on a trunk, grasses, pastures, and legumes. Among drugs, it rules those that serve as both food and medicine, such as cinnamon, long pepper, ginger, and Chinese cinnamon. It rules anything whose temperament is cold and moist, whose taste is bland, and whose color is white or green. Among animals, it rules grey horses, mules, donkeys, cattle, rabbits, and birds that are light and swift in the air, as well as every animal that is formed in the air and feeds on it, every white bird, water birds, white snakes, and white worms. Among colors, it rules those composed of yellow and blond. Its symbol is ☾ <note>The Moon</note>.

Know that the **۞Head۞** <note>The North Node of the Moon, or Rahu</note> is increasing by nature; if it is with the "Fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it increases their luck, and if it is with the "Infortunes" <note>malefic planets like Saturn or Mars</note>, it increases their misfortune. The **۞Tail۞** <note>The South Node of the Moon, or Ketu</note> is decreasing by nature; if it is with the "Fortunes," it decreases their luck, and if it is with the "Infortunes," it decreases their misfortune. So be one who knows this.

<meta>This page continues the astrological and talismanic instructions, moving from the physical attributes of the zodiac signs to the specific visual iconography of the seven planets as attributed to Aristotle. It details the ritual requirements for celestial magic, including appropriate attire and the chemical composition of planetary inks.</meta>

<page-num>160</page-num>

Aristotle described, in his book titled *The Book of Lamps and Banners*, the images of the planets for Alexander when he imparted to him the subtle points of this science. He depicted them as follows:

The image of **Saturn** is that of a black man wrapped in a green cloak with his head covered, holding a sickle in his hand.

**Jupiter** is the image of a man wearing fine garments, seated upon a throne <note>original: *kursi*; literally a chair or stool, but implying a seat of authority</note>.

**Mars** is the image of a man riding a lion, holding a long spear in his hand.

**The Sun** is the image of a beardless, handsome youth with a crown on his head and a spear in his hand. Beside him is a figure with a human head and hands—its arms and hands raised—but its body is like that of a horse with four legs <note>This describes a Centaur-like figure, often associated with the solar decans or specific degrees in medieval iconography</note>.

**Venus** is the image of a young woman; in her right hand is a comb and in the other an apple, and her hair is let down loose.

**Mercury** is the image of a naked man riding an eagle, and he is writing.

**The Moon** is the image of a knight riding a rabbit.

Among the teachings he deposited in that book, after categorizing gems and stones according to the planets, was this: 
"O Alexander, whenever you perform a ritual for a planet, make the physical object you are working with suitable for that planet. As for clothing, if you go out to perform a task under a certain <term>Ascendant</term><note>The *Tali'* or Rising Sign; the zodiac sign appearing on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</note>, wear the clothes that resemble that sign. Strengthen the 'Lord of the Ascendant' as much as you can, and weaken the Seventh House, because the Ascendant represents the seeker <note>The person performing the magic or asking the question</note> and the Seventh represents the thing sought."

The colors of **Saturn** are all shades of black; if it is made of wool, it is superior. The colors of **Jupiter** are shades of green; if it is made of silk, it is superior. The colors of **Mars** are fiery reds; if it is embroidered or variegated silk, it is superior.

<column-break/>

<page-num>161</page-num>

And for him <note>likely referring to Mercury, continuing from the previous page's logic</note> are the colors green, dark grey, dusty-grey, and yellow. Among tastes, he rules sweetness. Among locations, he rules places of running water, seas, and places where wine is sold. Among gems, he rules glass and its likeness. Among plants, he rules tall trees. Among animals, he rules humans and every creature with an ugly or strange form, such as those spirits described as Jinn or demons.

**Pisces** rules the feet, their extremities, and their nerves. Among colors, it rules green, white, and any multi-colored pattern. Among tastes, it rules sourness. Among locations, it rules places of worship, riverbanks, lakes, thickets, and seashores. Among gems, it rules pearls, white rubies <note>original: *yaqut abyad*; likely referring to white sapphires or clear precious stones</note>, shells, crystal, and all aquatic minerals. Among plants, it rules trees of moderate height and water plants. Among animals, it rules water birds and aquatic creatures. These qualities are specific to the planets and the zodiac signs, and the need for this knowledge is urgent.

## Chapter (3)

The planets have specific inks used for their particular operations:

**Saturn's** ink is made from burnt wool.
**Jupiter's** ink is made from <term>verdigris</term><note>A green pigment (copper acetate) formed by the action of acetic acid on copper</note>.
**Mars's** ink is made from <term>cinnabar</term><note>A bright red mineral consisting of mercury sulfide</note>.
**The Sun's** ink is made from yellow <term>arsenic</term><note>Specifically orpiment, a deep yellow-orange arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment to imitate gold</note>.
**Venus's** ink is made from saffron.
**Mercury's** ink is a mixture made from lac, arsenic, and verdigris.
**The Moon's** ink is made from white lead <note>original: *al-bayad*; literally "the white," referring to white pigments like ceruse</note>.

❊ **Taurus** ❊ The first face of it: its ink is a smoky, inky gray. The procedure is to collect soot in the top of an <term>alembic</term> <note>original: *athal*; an alchemical vessel used for sublimation or distillation</note> and add to it gum and fish glue—one <term>dirham</term> <note>a unit of weight, approximately 3.12 grams</note> per ounce—and a little <term>borax</term> <note>original: *barwaq*</note>, then draw with it. The second face: its ink is golden yellow. The recipe is to take <term>gallnuts</term> <note>original: *‘afs*; tannin-rich growths used to make permanent ink</note>, crush them, and remove the blackness from their centers. Soak them in enough water to cover them, then mix this water with a red liquid extracted from <term>lac</term> <note>original: *lakk*; a resinous secretion of insects used as a red dye</note>. Add a little gum to them and draw with it. The third face: its ink is yellow, as previously described.

❊ **Gemini** ❊ The first face of it: its ink is golden, its recipe having been mentioned. The second face: its ink is red, made from the distillate of red vitriol and <term>cinnabar</term> <note>original: *zinjafur*; mercuric sulfide, a bright red pigment</note>, adding a little gum to them. The third face: its ink is yellow, as we have already mentioned.

❊ **Cancer** ❊ The first face of it: white, as previously described. The second face: golden yellow, as previously described. The third face: black like the ink of the first face, except that its <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: *zaj*; metallic sulfates used in ink making</note> is equal in measure to the gallnuts.

The first of these is ❊ **Aries** ❊. The first face of it: its ink is tawny <note>original: *ashqar*; often meaning blond or reddish-brown</note>. Place a little gum in the distillate and draw with it. The third face: its ink is white, made from talc and egg white.

and a little gum. The second face is black; the procedure is to take good Persian ink,
<margin>15</margin> gum, and gallnuts—one part of each—and half a part of burnt paper. All of this is crushed,
sifted, and kneaded with egg white, then formed into pellets and dried. When needed, it is dissolved and drawn with.
The third face is green, made from animal gall and a little gum; write with it.
<margin>18</margin> ❊ **Pisces** ❊ The first face of it is ash-gray, made from <term>zircon</term> <note>original: *zarqun*</note> broken with white and a little [gum].

### Chapter 4

<margin>6</margin> Know, O observer, that I saw an extraordinary book by **Ja'far al-Basri** <note>likely an early scholar of the occult or a pseudonym for a Shi'ite esotericist</note> which he named *The Hidden Book* (*Al-Kitab al-Makhzun*). It was kept secret by one of his companions, who would not show it to anyone for fear of their peering into its secrets. I found that Ja’far had divided the verses of the **Noble Book** <note>The Quran</note> among the **seven planets**.

<margin>9</margin> He claimed that this was done by a specific design and that there are many secrets in understanding it. He further claimed that through this division, one can extract the **Hidden Name** <note>The "Greatest Name of God," believed in mystical traditions to grant the user power over reality</note> which God has deposited in the hearts of the saints and the wise who possess gnosis. This is a symbolic code of his.

<margin>12</margin> He also claimed that from this division, one can extract and learn the duration of **dynasties** and **celestial cycles** <note>original: *al-adwar al-falakiyya*; long-term astrological periods that determine the rise and fall of kingdoms</note>. This is why the **unpointed letters** <note>original: *al-huruf ghayr al-mu'ajama*; the mysterious disjointed letters like ALM or YS found at the start of certain Quranic chapters</note> were fixed at the beginning of some chapters. He argued they are evidence of the length of the **Cycle of Venus**; by dividing by some of those letters and taking their sum, one learns the length of its remaining time, its expiration, and the beginning of the cycle that follows it in

<margin>15</margin> governance. He claimed that through this knowledge, one can reach an understanding of the effects and wonders that will manifest in the renewed cycle of every planet. This is a marvelous system and code.

...speech that is not meant to be taken at face value, for it possesses an inner spiritual meaning. In general, it is a term with two aspects: the **manifest** and the **hidden**, designed for a specific benefit or wisdom. For this reason, it has been said that the Quran has both an inner and an outer dimension. These two descriptions are relative; for what is manifest may be manifest to one thing and hidden to another. A thing is not manifest and hidden from a single perspective; rather, it is manifest from one angle—in relation to a specific perception—and hidden from another. Indeed, appearance and concealment are defined only in relation to the faculties of perception.

For this reason, God Almighty is **Hidden** if sought through the perception of the senses or the storehouse of the imagination, but **Manifest** if sought through the storehouse of the intellect by way of logical deduction. If it is asked: "His being hidden in relation to the senses is clear, but His being manifest to the intellect is obscure, since the 'manifest' is that which is not doubted and which people do not differ in perceiving—yet God is the subject of great doubt among creation—so how can He be manifest?" 

Then know: He is hidden despite His manifestation only because of the *intensity* of His manifestation. His manifestation is the very cause of His concealment; His light is the veil of His light. As the saying goes, "Everything that exceeds its limit turns into its opposite." 

An example of this is that the signs and proofs of God are too many for anyone but God to count. Within a person's own soul are lessons and signs that should suffice. They are all evidences that leave the sight humbled. Just as an excess of physical light dazzles the eye until it turns away humbled, so too the intensity of His manifestation is the cause of His being hidden. Thus, He is hidden from them due to the strength of His appearance. He is the **Manifest**, than whom nothing is more manifest, and the **Hidden**, than whom nothing is more hidden. He is the one who is concealed by His essence and revealed through His signs. 

Know that the reason the letters upon which speech revolves are twenty-eight is because this number represents a **perfect individual**, composed of both spirit and body. The fourteen letters that appear at the beginnings of the Chapters <note>original: "Swar"; the 114 chapters of the Quran</note> represent the station of the **spirit**. Just as the spirit is subtle and hidden, the secret of these letters is hidden. This is also the number of the hidden lunar mansions. The fourteen letters that do not appear at the beginnings of the Chapters represent the station of the **body** and the station of...

"Abu Bakr ibn Wahshiyya" <note>A famous 10th-century scholar who claimed to translate ancient Nabataean secrets</note> related matters concerning the Nabataeans <margin>12</margin> in the book he titled "The Nabataean Agriculture" <note>Al-Filaha al-Nabatiyya, a major source for medieval occultism</note>, in which he spoke at great length. I will provide you with some of it. Along with that, they possess wondrous compounds that spread the actions and influences of the planets into the air after the air has been mixed with the fiery power. The air then carries the spiritual essence <note>original: "ruhaniyya"</note> of that compound to the hidden spiritual essence within the target person. Since air is a body through which alone other bodies have life, it is <margin>15</margin> the medium for the occurrence of "giving and receiving" <note>the transmission of magical influence</note>, combined with the resolve of the practitioner and the stripping away of his own desires from anything that might taint them. For the air is more pervasive in its power than any trick of a resolute person could penetrate. Therefore, no one is able to divert what has been made of these things, because they are celestial, spiritual matters, linked one to another. <margin>18</margin> They also have works involving incantations <note>original: "ruqa"</note> composed of human limbs, plants, and other generated things.

...those with hooves and paws <note>This continues from the previous page's list of animal types</note>. Among them are intermediate animals, birds of prey, land predators, and those close to speech <note>likely referring to primates or parrots</note>. Just as man is the link between animal <margin>3</margin> and angel, so too is the fish a link between birds and other animals, and the seashell is a link between animal and mineral. It possesses only two senses due to the dominance of the element of earth within it, and it is similar to plants. Man, however, has taken equally from every element; thus, he is the most balanced of animals, <margin>6</margin> standing upright and immersed in the air with a balanced temperament. 

If it is asked how this is so, know that every element has a specific animal associated with it: birds are associated with the air, fish with the water, and the Jinn and rebellious spirits with fire—this refers to "universal fire." As for "particular fire," it is unique <margin>9</margin> to the salamander <note>original: "samandal," a mythical creature believed to live in fire</note> and its ilk. The earth is the domain of minerals and plants. Although all elements interact and are affected by one another—for the elements <term>al-istiqsat: from the Greek 'stoicheia,' the four basic building blocks of matter</term> influence each other—each element has a specialty. The bird’s <margin>12</margin> life and will are in flying through the air; the fish is the same in water; the hidden, rebellious animal <note>the Jinn</note> is in the fire; and all weight resides in the earth, which is the lowest of its sisters. 

Perhaps one might ask: How can Jinn be imagined in fire? Let it be known that in the human body there is a model of this: anger, the desire for evil, and revenge are simply the result of an excessive burning of the fire-element in the <margin>15</margin> body. When this fire becomes excessive, it takes the place of the demons that our eyes cannot perceive. If it is in balance, they are like angels that our eyes cannot envision. Thus, angels exist within us and in the "Highest Assembly" above the world of physical existence. Similarly, the Jinn attributed to fire exist in <margin>18</margin> fire. For man is a **microcosm** <note>original: "alam saghir," meaning "little world"</note>, and nothing exists in the Upper World except that it possesses...

<margin>3</margin> He took some dry garlic, crushed it, and kneaded it with wax. From this, he fashioned a figure of the boy and dressed it in clothes resembling the boy’s own. Then, he took a clay jar and fixed seven sticks into it, taken from the branches of the Myrtle, Willow, Pomegranate, Quince, Mulberry, Laurel, and Plane tree <note>The plane tree, or Platanus orientalis, was often used in ancient landscaping and medicine</note>. He first mounted my figure in the jar, followed by the figure of the boy, placing it with its back to me. He focused 
<margin>6</margin> on performing this action while Venus was in opposition to Mars, which was a fortunate alignment. He continued to repeat this every day at the same hour he had first set it up. Gradually, the figure of the boy began to tilt toward me until, on the "Day of the Trine" <term>al-Tathlith: an astrological aspect where two planets are 120 degrees apart, considered highly harmonious</term>, the face of his figure had turned toward mine, and their faces were pressed together. Then he turned it away from my figure,
<margin>9</margin> covered the top of the jar, and ordered me to bury it under a hearth containing a small amount of embers. He then burned a piece of Sandarac <note>original: "Sandarus," a fragrant resin from the Tetraclinis tree used in incense and varnish</note> and spoke certain words in the Indian language which I later memorized from him. When he finished his speech, he said, "Retrieve the jar." I took it out and found that the figure of the boy had moved as if it had been made to do so. He then removed both figures.
<margin>12</margin> No sooner had we settled than the door of the place opened and the youth entered. He did not leave our side for ten days while his family searched for him, for the figure representing him remained hidden under that hearth. When the Indian man saw this, he said, "Now we shall release him, since you have witnessed what I promised you." Then he took seeds of 
<margin>15</margin> the Chaste Tree <term>Habb al-Faqd: seeds of the Vitex agnus-castus, used in medieval science to suppress or alter physical desires</term>, kneaded them with wax, and made a wick from it. He lit it under that hearth after removing the figures and separating them; he did this to show me the wonders of his craft. He then spoke other words, and the boy, who had been like a drunken man, suddenly woke from his stupor. He opened his eyes and asked, "Will you give me permission to leave?"
<margin>18</margin> We gave him permission, and he departed. Word of this spread because he had been missing for days, so we moved from that place because of the incident.

I was aided in its composition by several books—two hundred and twenty-four in number—from the books of the masters of this craft. He must know that this nature possesses what we have already alluded to in terms of color, taste, and smell. He should then manage the exterior of the body with that color and smell by adopting that color as clothing and that smell as perfume. He should manage the interior of his body with that nature and taste by adopting them as food. This food should be an addition to his previous food, as the previous food was what maintained the health of the body.

For example, you might mount it on the image of a lion or a snake if you intend by it warfare or the intimidation of enemies; or on a bird if you intend escape from terrors; or as one sitting on a pulpit if you intend the magnification of status, glory, and the elevation of rank, and such things.

If you do not know the ruling planet of a person's birth—whether for all people or just one—we should fashion seven images from the seven stones that are assigned to the seven planets. These are:
<margin>3</margin> **Antimony**, which belongs to Saturn; **Peridot** <note>original: *al-zabarjad*, often translated as chrysolite or emerald in medieval texts</note>, which belongs to Jupiter; **Arsenic** <note>likely realgar or orpiment, used for its planetary color associations</note>, which belongs to Mars; **Al-Bazadi** <note>a red gemstone, possibly a variety of garnet or spinel</note>, which belongs to the Sun; **Hematite** <margin>6</margin> <note>original: *al-shadhana*, literally "bloodstone"</note>, which belongs to Venus; **Talc**, which belongs to Mercury; and **Crystal**, which belongs to the Moon. Or, one may use whatever substitutes belong to these planetary divisions. We should fashion an image from each of these stones during the hour of the planet to which that stone belongs. These seven images shall bear the **cross** mentioned previously. We specified that <margin>9</margin> it be a cross because we have already stated that everything connects to its own likeness and repels what is unlike it. We wish to connect the celestial **spirituality** <note>original: *al-ruhaniyya*, referring to the divine or astral energy associated with a planet</note> to a form of its own likeness. Yet, we do not know the specific form of this spirituality, nor do we find proof that the form of a spirit is that of a human or any other creature. <margin>12</margin> This statement is one of their symbolic riddles, for they built this science upon images. Rather, he [the author] was pointing to the universal meaning in his work. He then said: We see that every form of plant differs from one another, as do the forms of animals and minerals. How then can they know <margin>15</margin> the form of a spirit? For this reason, we shaped it in the form of a **cross**. This is because every physical body falls under this shape; the surface of a body consists of length and breadth, and the very form of length and breadth is the cross. We chose it for this reason: to be a shape that the spirituality does not repel.

# Chapter (6)

And this science—may God aid you—its practice and understanding cannot be achieved except by one whose nature <margin>3</margin> is suited for it. To this **Aristotle** alluded in the **"Book of the Stomachis"** <note>original: *al-Isṭamākhīs*, a magical-philosophical text attributed to Aristotle in the Arabic tradition, often dealing with the "Perfect Nature"</note> when he said that the **Perfect Nature** <term>Perfect Nature: *al-Ṭibāʿ al-Tāmm*, a Hermetic concept referring to a celestial twin or personal guardian spirit that reveals hidden wisdom to the philosopher</term> is a power for the philosopher that increases his knowledge and wisdom. For the sages, regarding this **spirituality**— <margin>6</margin> and this is the secret established among them, which no one else discovers—there are varying shares. It is the hidden secret in wisdom, for there was no subtle or grand gate of wisdom that the sages revealed to their disciples or circulated <margin>9</margin> among themselves through correspondence or inquiry, except for this hidden secret which is the spirituality of the **Perfect Nature**. The sages used to call this spirituality **Tamāghīs Baghdīswād** and **Ghadās Nūfānāghādīs**. These four words are the names of this spirituality which they would invoke <margin>12</margin> when in need of it, and they refer to the **Perfect Nature**. **Hermes** mentioned: "When I desired to extract the science of the **Secret of Creation** <note>original: *Sirr al-Khalīqa*, a famous Hermetic work attributed to 'Balinas' or Apollonius of Tyana</note> and its nature, I came upon a dark passage, filled with darkness and winds. Begin with the East, then the West, then the South <note>original: *al-qiblī*, referring to the direction of prayer, which is south in the region where these texts were popularized</note>, and finally the North <note>original: *al-baḥrī*, literally 'towards the sea'</note>. Then begin with the oils: almond oil for the East next to the cup of drink, then walnut oil for the West, then clarified butter <note>original: *samn* (ghee)</note> for the South, then vinegar for the North. I found this distribution in the **"Book of the Stomachis"** <gloss>a)</gloss>. Then take a candle, light it, and place it in the center of the table. Next, take two censers filled with charcoal. In one, burn mastic and frankincense; in the other, burn moist aloe wood. Then stand facing the East and repeat seven times: **Tamāghīs Baghdīswād wa-Ghadās Nūfānāghādīs**. Then, following that, say: "I call upon you, O powerful, spiritual, and exalted souls, who are the wisdom of the wise, the discernment of the discerning, and the knowledge of the scholars. Answer me, attend to me, and bring me close to your guidance. Direct me with your wisdom, support me with your strength, make me understand what I do not understand, teach me what I do not know, and give me sight for what I do not see."

And his status with me increased when I revealed that to him <note>Aristotle is referring to his relationship with Alexander and the sharing of these secrets</note>, though I had not informed him of it previously. So, commit yourself to this invocation at the very start of your journey. Recite the names of these spiritual beings <term>Spiritualities: *ruhaniyyat*, the celestial or energetic forces associated with the stars</term>, for they will grant you success, empower you, give you victory over whoever opposes you, and humble whatever you find difficult. When you do this, do not neglect the matter of the stars, and do not travel except by their guidance. For the stars are the head of the world’s governance, and through them, the affairs of both the "Small World" <note>The Microcosm, or man</note> and the "Great World" <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe</note> are established.

Seek help from the four spiritualities of your star, which constitute the **Perfect Nature** <note>The *al-Tibā‘ al-Tāmm*, a personal guardian spirit or higher self in Hermetic tradition</note>. In the four names I have given you lies the Secret of Secrets. They became four because the natures <note>The four elements or temperaments</note> are four. Pray with them and commit to them at all times; flee to them in your affairs and in whatever is locked against you.

I have seen through your exalted star that you shall conquer Persia and kill its kings. At the first moment you depart from your lands for the land of Persia, you will encounter great hardship from them. When the matter exhausts you and you despair of victory, the spirituality of your **Perfect Nature**—connected to your star—will arise upon your invocation. Turn to it when the struggle weighs heavily upon you; it will connect with your star and then cast its radiant power upon the supporters, ministers, and commanders of the King of Persia. It will pull the affection of their hearts toward you. It will signal to them to kill their king and to offer you their hearing and obedience. They will then awake and gather in their assembly, and their word will be united upon you. The affection of their hearts will be joined to you; they will agree to kill the King and will bring you his head, hearing and obeying you.

I see for you victory and dominance over all kings; they will fear you and seek peace treaties. I also see your death in a "land of iron and a sky of gold" <note>A famous prophecy regarding Alexander's death; legend says he died resting on his armor (iron) under a golden canopy or shield (gold)</note>, after you have uprooted nations, killed kings, and collected wealth and treasures. This is what I see from the strength of your star, the dominance of your kingdom, and the spirituality of your **Perfect Nature**. This is the text of **Aristotle’s** speech on that matter.

It helped them in their year, their wisdom, the management of their affairs, and the success of their guidance. It repelled the evil plots of wicked people from their kingdoms. It was a help to them in kingship and in unifying the word of their subjects in obedience.

"This spirituality"—he says to **Alexander**—"O King, which governs you: I have told you its names and revealed to you the hidden secret within it. Were it not for the King’s high station..."

### ->Section (7)<-

Among the practices of the Sabians <note>The Sabians of Harran were a community of pagans in Upper Mesopotamia known for preserving Hellenistic science, star-worship, and Hermetic philosophy.</note> is what was mentioned by "al-Tabari" the Astrologer <note>Likely Umar ibn al-Farrukhan al-Tabari, a prominent translator and astrologer in the early Abbasid court.</note> concerning the drawing down of planetary powers. He said: "What I have found from the leaders of the Sabians and the servants of the temples regarding the bringing down of the planets and their service is what I shall mention. They said: If you wish to commune with a planet or ask it for a need, you must first perceive the fear of God Almighty, purify your heart from corrupt beliefs, cleanse your garments of filth, and make your soul sincere and pure. Then, look at the need you are requesting—to which of the seven planets it belongs, and from the nature of which celestial planet it originates. Direct yourself to that celestial planet whose nature corresponds to that need. Put on its specific clothing, burn its specific incense, and call upon it with its specific prayer, provided that the planet is within the boundaries that I shall delineate for you regarding its positions in the sphere. For if you do this, your need will be fulfilled and you will achieve the goal of your request."

As for Saturn, you ask him for needs related to venerable elders, leaders, kings, ancients, ascetics, owners of estates, contractors, heirs, stewards, agents, farmers, builders, slaves, thieves, fathers, and grandfathers. If you are grieving or afflicted by a disease of black bile <term>Black Bile: One of the four humors, traditionally associated with melancholy and the influence of the planet Saturn</term>, or any matter belonging to his nature, then seek it according to what I delineate for you. Seek assistance for it through Jupiter, for he is the rectifier of what Saturn corrupts. Sometimes, a person might mistakenly seek a matter from one planet, and that planet then asks another planet so that the matter is concluded; therefore, do not ask for a matter except from the planet that is suitable for it.

---

<note>original: "Hoc capitulum edid. Dozy-De Goeje, Nouveaux documents pour l'étude de la religion des Harraniens..." This chapter was edited by Dozy and De Goeje in "New Documents for the Study of the Religion of the Harranians," Proceedings of the 6th Congress of Orientalists in Leiden.</note>

<column-break/>

The Perfect Nature <term>Perfect Nature: *Al-Tiba' al-Tamm*, a central concept in Hermeticism representing a personal guiding spirit or "Higher Self" that acts as an intermediary between the philosopher and the divine</term> establishes its ray within the soul. This ray then penetrates and falls upon the subtle powers of wisdom, attracting those powers through its radiance until it establishes them within the soul, which is its proper place—just as the rays of the sun attract the powers of the world and raise them into the atmosphere.

Socrates the Sage said: "The Perfect Nature is called the Sun of the Sage, its root and its branch." Hermes was asked: "By what means is wisdom attained?" He replied: "Through the Perfect Nature." It was said to him: "What is the root of wisdom?" He said: "The Perfect Nature." It was said to him: "What is the key to wisdom?" He said: "The Perfect Nature." It was then asked: "And what is the Perfect Nature?" He replied: "It is the spirituality of the philosopher that is connected to his star and governs him; it opens for him the locks of wisdom, teaches him what is difficult for him, reveals the truth to him, and grants him the keys to the gates in sleep and in wakefulness."

Thus, the Perfect Nature is to the philosopher like a sincere teacher who instructs a boy word by word; whenever the boy masters one gate of knowledge, the teacher leads him into another. That boy will never fear a deficiency in knowledge as long as that teacher remains with him, for he clarifies what is ambiguous, teaches what is difficult, and initiates instruction on things that were not even asked about. Such is the Perfect Nature for the philosopher. Know this. It is for this reason that we have said that this science—its knowledge and its practice—cannot be attained by a human, nor can its secrets be understood, except by one whose own nature is suited for it. This was the reason for citing the words of the sage Aristotle on this matter, so understand.

Ask Venus about the affairs of women, singing girls <term>Qiyan: Professional female entertainers, often enslaved, who were highly educated in music and literature</term>, slave girls, beardless youths and the pursuit of them, children, those who love children, lovers, people of passion, adulterers, those who engage in sodomy or female-female intimacy <note>The original terms 'liwaṭa' and 'sahaqat' refer to same-sex male and female acts respectively</note>, those who play all kinds of musical instruments, the flute-players, singers, the effeminate, the gender-nonconforming <term>Mukhannath: A historical category for individuals assigned male at birth who lived or dressed with feminine characteristics</term>, hermaphrodites, eunuchs, slaves, servants, young boys, and people of flattery and adulation. In general, ask her about artists, jesters, spouses, mothers, maternal aunts, and younger sisters. Seek help for these matters through Mars, for she is infatuated with him and leans toward him.

Ask Mercury about the affairs of scribes, accountants, engineers, astrologers, orators, the eloquent, the gifted in speech, scholars, philosophers, wise men, theologians, men of letters, poets, the children of kings, ministers, directors of administrative bureaus, officials, tax collectors, merchants, and practitioners of both theoretical and practical crafts. Ask him about adversaries, litigants, slaves, hermaphrodites, young boys, male and female attendants, younger brothers, craftsmen, engravers, painters, goldsmiths, and whatever resembles his nature.

Ask the Moon about the affairs of kings, deputies, heirs apparent, land-tax officials, couriers, messengers, travelers, migrants, peasants, builders, engineers, land surveyors, agents, village headmen <term>Dihqan: The landed gentry or local administrative elite in the Persian-influenced world</term>, sailors, and those who work with water. Ask her about the common folk and the masses, sorcerers, wealthy women and those who are pregnant, royal servants, mothers, maternal aunts, and elder sisters. The intent is that you should not ask a planet for something that is not within its nature; know this.

For the incense and its preparation: take sandarac, liquid storax, "pigeon’s foot" <note>likely *Echium italicum* or *Fumaria*, known in Arabic as *Rijl al-Hamama*</note>, and peony root—which is a wood that, when broken, reveals a cross inside, no matter how it is broken—sweet flag <term>Qasab dharira: an aromatic reed used in ancient perfumes and oils</term>, pine resin, 
<margin>3</margin> and juniper berries, one part of each in equal measure. After grinding them, knead the mixture with wine and shape it into wicks to be used when needed. <margin>6</margin> hot, moist, moderate, and beautiful; the Knower, the Truthful, master of truth, justice, and equity; the pious, the wise in religion, the ascetic, the powerful, the one of great ambition, the reformer, the noble, the high, the great, the subduer, the granter of honor, the faithful to covenants, the sincere in love, and the noble of nature. <margin>9</margin> father, by the right of your noble and beautiful character and your precious deeds, to do such-and-such for me, O source of goodness and granter of requests."

You should wear the clothes

...in Arabic, O Mushtari <note>Jupiter</note>; in Persian, O Birjis; in the foreign tongue, O Hurmuz <note>Middle Persian name for Jupiter/Ormuzd</note>; in Greek, O Zawush <note>original: *Zawush*, a corruption of the Greek *Zeus*</note>; and in Indian, O Wahsafat <note>original: *Wahsafat*, likely derived from the Sanskrit *Brihaspati*</note>. ### Regarding the speech and communion with Jupiter that requires no incense
This is used for safety at sea from the great power [of the waves]. A group of practitioners of this art have mentioned it, and **al-Razi** mentioned it in his *Book of Divine Science* <note>Abu Bakr al-Razi (c. 865–925 CE), known in the West as Rhazes, was a Persian polymath; this refers to his philosophical/metaphysical works</note> according to a report of his. It is that you face him while he is in the middle of the sky and say: "Peace be upon you, O noble, illustrious, and great star; the compassionate one who oversees the affairs of the worlds, the one who attends to the spirits of the pure, and the rescuer of the drowning who cry for help in the depths of the seas. May you pour upon us your light, your spirit, and your spirituality, through which our circumstances may improve, our outcomes may be good, and the filth of [material] nature may be washed from us. Amen." The sign of acceptance is the appearance of a lit candle before the one communing with him; this is the spirituality of Jupiter.

### Regarding the "Greatest Speech" according to them, which encompasses all his actions and powers
It is that you say, while facing him:
"Peace be upon you, O happy and noble star, who is noble of nature, illustrious in rank, and of great importance. O blessed lord, <term>Hot and Moist</term> <note>Jupiter's primary elemental qualities in medieval astrology</note>, <term>Airy</term>, moderate, beautiful, and wise. The truthful in love, the jurist in religion, the possessor of truth, certainty, manifest luck, trust, faith, justice, equity, and piety. The wise, the sublime, the radiant, the righteous, and the compassionate. One of great ambition, the reformer, the high, the generous, the subduer, the granter of honor, the fulfiller of covenants, the sincere in promise, the complete and perfect..."

Master of the skilled tongue, the lover of marriage and goodness, the hater of evil, the commander of right and the forbidder of wrong. 

Peace be upon you, O star supported by mercy and benevolence, who oversees the affairs of the worlds and guides the spirits of the pure. The reliever of terrors and the rescuer in the depths of the sea for the drowning who cry for help. May you pour upon us, our children, and our families your light, your spirit, your ease, and the light of your noble spirituality—which is connected to the celestial powers—by which you may guard our affairs, increase our wealth, and repel from us all the anxieties of our livelihood in this world, so that our living may be fertile, prosperous, good, righteous, and blessed. May you heal our bodies through the power of your spirituality, lengthen our lifespans, grant us health from all maladies and pains, and repel from us all afflictions, whether small or great. Cast upon us, by the power of your noble, illustrious, and virtuous spirituality, that which will earn us awe, honor, glory, and greatness. Create for us acceptance on earth among all people, and repel from us those who wish us harm..."

...generally, [protecting] him from those diseases until another year. The world shall be subjected to him, every difficult thing made easy for him, and awe shall be instilled for him in the hearts of all the world—especially if the one presiding over <note>original: *al-mustawlī*, meaning the one in control or the dominant influence</note> this invocation is this planet <note>Jupiter</note>. Know that repentance, humility, and rubbing the forehead upon the ground are among the things that assist in a speedy response.

As for **Mars** <note>original: *al-Marrikh*</note>, if you wish to commune with him, wear red clothing and a red turban. Gird yourself with a sword, put on as much armor as possible, and appear in the guise of soldiers, warriors, and people of ill-intent, or in the dress of idol-worshipers, for he is the master of their cycles. Wear a copper ring and burn incense in a copper brazier. The recipe for his incense is to take <term>Dahsht resin<note>A psychoactive or aromatic resin used in medieval sorcery to induce altered states</note></term>, male frankincense, aloe, <term>lemongrass<note>original: *idhkhir*, an aromatic desert grass</note></term>, <term>euphorbium<note>original: *faribun*, a caustic plant resin associated with the heat of Mars</note></term>, and long pepper—one equal part of each. After crushing them, knead them with human blood <note>A common, albeit macabre, element in medieval martial magic intended to create a 'sympathetic' link to the nature of Mars as the god of war</note>. Form them into wicks, set them aside, and use them as incense when needed. When you wish to commune with him, approach him with sharpness and boldness. Face him while he is in the middle of the sky, as you do for other planets, and say while burning the incense:

"O Virtuous Master, Hot and Dry, Brave of heart, Shedder of blood, Stirrer of the masses, Strong of mention, Subduer, Victor, Reckless, Sharp one; Master of evil, torment, striking, imprisonment, lying, slander, and obscenity; the One of little concern, the Killer, the Lone, the Stranger, the Bearer of arms, the One of much copulation, the Powerful of thought in subjugation and victory, the Bringer of war, the Helper of the weak <note>Manuscript C notes 'the weak', while others imply 'the strong' or 'the bold'</note>, the Redresser of evil, the Avenger against the wicked—I ask you by your stations and your courses in your sphere, and by your victory, and by Him who preferred you and made you an avenger..."

<margin>12</margin> As for its Lesser Incense and the "Standing" for it: when you desire this, do as I have commanded you regarding

<margin>15</margin> formed into pellets, and set aside. When needed, burn it as incense while you say: "Peace be upon you, O

the Exalted, the Noble, the Sovereign, the Gatherer of Beauty, the Pure, the Sage, the Gatherer of Wealth.

As for the "Standing" for the Sun and its <term>address</term><note>original: 'munajat', a private or intimate conversation with a deity</note>: this is required for anyone who wishes to connect

## Mercury (Utarid)
As for **Mercury** <note>Arabic: 'Utarid'. In the astral tradition, Mercury governs intellect, writing, and administration.</note>, when you wish to commune with him, perform his invocation, and meet his conditions—and this is if you have a need concerning scribes or officials of the state departments <term>Dīwāns: administrative offices or bureaus</term>—then seek out Mercury when the Moon is in conjunction <note>original: 'mujasadan', literally 'embodied' or in close physical aspect</note> with him. Ask for your need by dressing in the attire of scribes in all your affairs. Wear a ring made of his metals—**solidified mercury** <note>original: 'al-zi’baq al-ma’qud'. Alchemically treated mercury made solid; this was considered the most noble metal of Mercury.</note> is the most honorable of them, and it was with this that **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of hermetic wisdom and magic</note> used to seal. Approach him with your face quickly, with cheerfulness and eloquence, while you are sitting upon the "Chair of the Sages"—for he is the guide of their cycles. In your hand, hold a book as if you are writing. Place the incense before you in a censer made of one of his metals. Then, offer the incense while saying:

"Peace be upon you, O Mercury! O virtuous, truthful, wise, and speaking Master! O understanding one, the debater, the scholar of every art, the accountant, the scribe! Owner of good character, knower of the news of the heavens and the earth, the noble lord who knows little of [earthly] joy..."

### The Composition of the Incense
This is the description of how to make the incense: **Raw Aloeswood**, **Suk** <term>Suk: a compounded incense base usually made of gallnuts, dates, and honey</term>, **Costus**, **Saffron**, **Labdanum**, **Mastic**, **Poppy shells**, **Willow leaves**, and **Lily root**. Take one part of each, grind them, knead them with rose water, form them into beads <note>original: 'yubandaq', meaning to roll into small pellets or pills</note>, and use them.

## Venus (al-Zahra)
As for the invocation of **Venus** <note>Arabic: 'al-Zahra', the Bright One.</note> for attracting love, affection, and intimacy: dress in her attire and burn this incense for her: **Suk**, **Storax**—five ounces of each—**Raisins**, **Male Frankincense**, and **Mastic**—two and a half ounces of each—**Indian Malabathrum** <note>original: 'Sadhaj Hindi', an aromatic leaf similar to cinnamon</note>, **Mahaleb cherry**, **Amomum** <note>original: 'Hamama', an aromatic plant used in ancient perfumery</note>, and **Lily root**—one ounce of each. Knead the whole mixture with "pure water," form into beads, and use them during your communion with her. You shall say:

"O Spirit of Love and System of Intimacy! O stirrer of the spirituality of desire and arouser of the power of pleasure! O improver of the essence of creatures and bringer together of the whims of estranged spirits! You are the source of marriage and the establishment of lineage, the one who inclines souls and connects them toward those who attract them. You endear whoever seeks love from you. O beautiful, compassionate, and intimate Venus! The one you attract submits to you, and the one you incline does not oppose you. 

I ask you—by your names, the names of your Creator, the one who makes you move in your sphere, by your light, and by the light of your authority—to turn toward me. For I complain of my distress regarding **so-and-so** <note>original: 'fulan', a placeholder for the target's name</note> toward me, and what I suffer from his desertion, his distance, his poor companionship, his haste to cut me off, and his deliberate opposition to me. O ultimate hope of those who seek support through her, and the furthest goal of the longing one who takes refuge in her! I ask you to send a spirit from your spirituality and a power from your powers upon him. By it, may you draw his spirituality—which dwells in his heart, is rooted in his nature, and wanders through all his limbs—toward me with affection and compassion. Move him toward me with a powerful motion and agitation..."

[The following is the address to the Moon:]

The possessor of radiant light and shining brilliance, of joy, praise, and commendation; the fortunate King, the jurist in religion, the thinker upon all things, the world-wise, subtle in management; the lover of amusement, jest, and play; <margin>3</margin> the master of messengers and news, who keeps few secrets; the generous, noble, clement, and magnificent. You are the closest of the planets to us in your sphere, and the greatest of them in light and benefit. You are the one who joins the planets together and transmits <margin>6</margin> their lights, the one who rectifies what we find ominous—for by your soundness, all things are made sound, and by your corruption, all things are corrupted. You are the first of all things and the last, and to you belongs honor and nobility over all the planets <margin>9</margin> together. Thus, I ask you by the right of the Angel *Siliyail* <note>original: "Siliyail," the celestial governor assigned to the Moon</note>, who is entrusted with your affairs, that you have mercy on my humility and my supplication to you. I obey through the obedience of God and His authority; answer me in what I call upon you for, and what I desire from you. I call upon you by all your names: in Arabic as **Qamar**; in Persian as **Mah**; in Greek as **Samail** <note>original: "sama'il," likely a corruption of the Greek *Selene*</note>; in Roman as **Salini** <note>original: "salini," also derived from the Greek *Selene*</note>; and in Indian as **Som** <note>original: "som," referring to the lunar deity *Soma*</note>. So, answer me!

<margin>12</margin> Then, mention your specific need and fall down prostrate before it, repeating your words while in prostration. During all of this, you must be burning its specific incense, which is the **"Small Incense of the Hanifs"** <note>The "Hanifs" here refers to the Sabians of Harran, who preserved ancient pagan rituals under this label</note>. This is its description and its twenty-eight ingredients:

Cardamom, <term>asparagus</term> <note>original: "asfalaraghas," from the Greek *asparagos*</note>, liquid storax, mastic, and <term>storax</term> <note>a fragrant resin</note> (five ounces of each); elecampane, myrrh, lemon grass, and <term>dar shish'an</term> <note>an aromatic wood, possibly *Agnus Castus*</note>; <margin>15</margin> spikenard, costus, frankincense, and saffron (two ounces of each); fifty pumpkin seeds; henna roots (four ounces); lily root, Roman spikenard, Indian leaf, and pine nuts (three ounces of each); Persian galbanum, fruit of the <term>arak</term> <note>the toothbrush tree, *Salvadora persica*</note>, and leaves...

<margin>1</margin> ...Dried apples and rose blossoms (six ounces of each); two pounds of <term>fruit syrup</term> <note>original: "sharab al-rubb," a thick preserve or medicinal syrup</note>; two pounds of seedless raisins; five pounds of dates; five pounds of honey; and enough <term>aromatic wine</term> <note>original: "matbukh rihani," a cooked, herb-infused wine</note> <margin>3</margin> to knead the mixture after it has been crushed and pounded. Afterward, it is formed into pellets, stored, and used for fumigation when needed. 

The offering that is sacrificed to [Mercury] should be a small calf. You shall kindle a fire until <margin>6</margin> its smoke ascends into the upper atmosphere as previously described, then burn the calf within it. If it is a ewe, slaughter it and burn it in the same manner. Eat its liver after you have finished, and your need shall be fulfilled.

<margin>8</margin> This is the doctrine of the Sabians regarding the <term>planetary stations</term> <note>original: "qiyamat," referring to the ritual standing or the astrological positions</note> and the offerings made to them when they are compelled by urgent matters. Every planet, according to them, grants what is within its nature to give; if it is a <term>benefic</term> <note>a planet that brings good fortune, like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it grants fortune, and if its opposite, then the opposite. In their method of petitioning, they intend for the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> <note>the planet ruling the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> to be in conjunction with the [target] planet, and for the ruling planet to be "oriental" <note>rising before the sun</note> and in a favorable quarter <margin>12</margin> of its <term>epicycle</term> <note>a small circular orbit used in ancient astronomy to explain planetary motion</note>. When it is oriental, your need is made easy. At night, these works are more effective and the powers are more closely connected. Do not ask a planet for something that is not within its nature to provide, for that leads to a bad and loathsome outcome.

<margin>15</margin> The Sabians to this day continue to use these ritual stations. They hold regarding the worship of the planets certain shocking views, including the sacrifice of a child. Whenever the sphere of the world ascends by eight degrees and descends by the same, they sacrifice a child. They claim that **Hermes** commanded them to do this—he who is called <margin>18</margin> among them **"Atras Maghastus"** <note>A corruption of "Hermes Trismegistus," the "Thrice-Great"</note>, meaning "The Triple in Wisdom," because he was a king, a prophet, and a sage. In their prayers in their temples, they do not sacrifice rams that are fully grown, nor those that are black...

To the Sun belongs specifically the preservation of the whole. He was released from his bonds, and his mother ransomed him with that rooster; she slaughtered it on his behalf and opened his eyes. He looked upon the likeness of the bird that had snatched away his sight, then he fell and was seized by a shudder. His mother then took him and threw a cloth over him. For this reason, no one who leaves the religion of the Sabians <note>A religious group of Harran often associated with ancient planetary worship and Hermeticism.</note> for another is able to reveal their secret, because the priest warns him that whoever discloses the secret of the Sabians or points it out shall die at that very hour. When the boy leaves the temple, he is sealed between his index finger and thumb with a signet ring bearing the image of a monkey and a hoopoe.

(a They say that the primary sacrifice for Saturn is the bull, as it possesses a "goodly nature." They venerate the crown of horns upon its head, saying it is the most charming <note>original: *amlah*, literally "saltiest," used idiomatically for beauty or grace</note> of beasts and the most worthy of sacrifice. They offer it specifically to him after feeding it grasses gathered by virgins at sunrise, who return by different paths to complete a secret entrusted to them. The calf must be without a single white hair. They place a golden chain over its eyes, reaching to the junction between its horns; they also attribute this practice to Hermes. When they wish to slaughter it, it does not resist them, nor do they need to bind it with a *fakhar*—which is a rope. They begin before it with incense and a prayer from the prayers of the Greeks. It then approaches the place of slaughter and places its horn on the edge of the <term>Mishkan</term> <note>An Aramaic term for a small, round ritual pit or basin.</note>, and the slaughterer kills it with a single stroke, without drawing the knife across it a second time. They then sever the head and place it upon the <term>Alatha</term> <note>An Aramaic word for an altar or fire-grate.</note>, where they interpret the movements of its tongue, ears, lips, and eyes. Then they look at the blood in the <term>Mishkan</term>, examining its yellowness, its foam, and the froth that swirls upon it.

...nor one with broken bones, a mutilated horn, or a missing eye. When they slaughter it, they remove the liver and examine it; if a scratch from the knife is found upon it, they say that the one offering the sacrifice will meet with a calamity. Then the liver is boiled and distributed in pieces to those attending the prayer in the temple.

They call Mars <term>Mara Samia</term> <note>Original: *Mara Samia*, likely meaning "The Blind Lord."</note>. He became blind according to them because of the intensity of his violence; when he intends evil, he cannot see. His image among them is that of a man holding a sword in his right hand and a bitter flame of fire in his left; with one he destroys the world by the sword, and with the other, he burns them with fire. For this reason, he is held in awe by them, and they offer sacrifices to him out of fear of his might. Their sacrifices to him occur when the Sun enters Aries, because it is his zodiacal house, and when it reaches Scorpio, they sacrifice to him as well.

And they have an examination for young boys. If a boy is born outside of Harran and then comes to Harran, they take him and enter him into their House of Secrets. They bring a piece of tamarisk wood in a censer, speak over it, and place it under his shirt. If it burns him from behind, they know he has a "disease" <note>A historical euphemism for being a passive partner in same-sex acts, considered a ritual disqualification.</note> and do not allow him to enter the place of prayer. If the fire burns him from the front, he also does not enter the place of prayer <note>Likely referring to active sodomy or adultery.</note>. This is for fear of him being a sinner of the back or a fornicator of the front. If he is tested and found free of defects, he is led into another dark temple. His eyes are bound, and the priest stands before him, placing a headband of red poplar upon his head. He is dressed in a <term>batit</term> <note>A ritual garment made from the skin of the animal sacrificed on his behalf.</note>. Beside his right foot, they place a basin containing fire, and beside his left foot, a basin containing water. His mother comes with a rooster and sits at the temple door. The priest takes a copper vessel in his hand containing a flame to strike awe into him. Once he has sworn him in and secured his oath with the Secret Prayer—which is—

They use this to infer the state of their dominion, for their state, according to them, is Saturnian; whatever <term>cycles</term><note>The Arabic *adwar* refers to astrological periods or planetary cycles believed to govern history.</note> Saturn begins, to him they return. This sacrifice occurs among them when the Sun moves into Taurus. This calf is mentioned in the Torah as the calf that escaped slaughter from the farm of the sons of Anun. <note>original: *Bani Anun*. Footnotes suggest variants like *Abun*, *Ayyub* (Job), or *Anun*.</note>

The Sabians also practice sprinkling wine and salt-dust in the face of every sacrifice. This is done so that the animal may be startled and shudder, causing the blood to spread through its body with the movement and become pure. They possess a "Vault of the Corpse" <note>original: *Khizanat al-Juththa*. Some manuscripts read "Vault of the Serpent" (*al-Hayya*).</note>, which is a temple that the common people do not enter, nor is anyone permitted to view it. Within it is a skillfully engineered pit equipped with various apparatuses. When the Sun enters Leo, they bring a fair-skinned, blond youth from the region of Cyprus—matching the description we provided for the image of the Head <note>Referencing a previous description of a ritual mask or idol.</note>. He is dressed and adorned, then led around to places of joy such as gardens, flowers, and aromatic herbs. He is given drink until he becomes intoxicated and is carried by night to that temple. He is placed in that pit and soaked in <term>sesame oil</term><note>original: *shiraj*, oil extracted from unroasted sesame.</note>. He is fed dried red roses, which they have prepared for this purpose, mixed into a mash containing seven ingredients: mustard, lentils, chickpeas, rice, mung beans, lupin, and wheat.

When the twenty-eighth day of the lunar month of Iyyar arrives, they administer a nasal medicinal vapor to him and make him sneeze after he has been blindfolded <note>The footnote references Dozy’s *Supplément* regarding the term for blindfolding.</note>. Then they take him out by night to a ruined path, sever his head from his body, and bury the body. They carry the head to the Monastery of Kadi <note>The location is uncertain; variants include *Kadan* or *Kadi*. This may refer to a specific Sabian cult site near Harran.</note> and place it on the back of an idol. The head then lets out a harsh howl. From its howling, they deduce whether the number of Sabians will increase or decrease, and whether political power will come to them or not. The one who established this law for them was a sage known as Bartheem the Brahmin <note>Footnotes show many variants: *Birnim*, *Barham*, *Barnac*. This reflects a medieval conflation of Indian Brahmanical traditions with Harranian Sabianism.</note>, who died in the land of India. For this reason, a group of people in India are called Brahmins. They have many such matters; were we to recount them all, the book would grow too long and we would stray from our purpose.

## Chapter (8)

As for the Nabataeans <note>In this context, "Nabataeans" refers to the indigenous inhabitants of Mesopotamia (Chaldeans/Arameans) rather than the people of Petra.</note>, they claim that all action in the world belongs to the Sun alone. However, they recognize that the Moon assists the Sun in its actions, though the Sun has no intrinsic need for the Moon or any other. Likewise, the **Seven Wandering Stars** <note>The five visible planets plus the Sun and Moon.</note> follow the Sun in action, obeying it willingly, prostrating to it, and praising it night and day. They are eternally constant in their obedience and persistence in seeking its pleasure in word and deed. Thus, for them, all actions belong to the Sun alone, while the rest of the Seven participate in some of its actions. Similarly, the fixed stars are its servants, praising and prostrating; they have a share in the actions without the Sun needing them. The sum of their prayers to the Sun and their speech regarding it is as follows:

-> Prayer, praise, thanksgiving, and glorification to our Lord, the Great, Illustrious, Radiant one—the Sun, giver of life to every living thing upon the face of the earth, enlightener of all with his light, and illuminator of the world with his radiance. He who sustains the worlds by his power, He of the High Station and Great Authority, who is filled with light, intellect, understanding, power, might, greatness, and goodness. He is the originator of every growing thing, the sustainer of all that is extended, the reviver of every living soul, and the strengthener of every strong one. He is noble in his actions, generous in his gifts, and powerful in his heaven. Peace be unto him, and glory, and magnification, and majesty, and praise, and worship. With his generosity, we seek him... <-
