One of the later practitioners of the <term>art of astrological judgments</term> <note>Arabic: *sina'at al-ahkam al-nujumiyya*, or judicial astrology—the practice of predicting earthly events based on the movements of stars and planets.</note> mentioned that he saw a "law" <note>Arabic: *namus*, here meaning a specific magical procedure or formula.</note> for invisibility recorded by these people. It involves waiting for the fourteenth night of 

<margin>18</margin> the lunar month, taking a rabbit marked with a sign, and slaughtering it while facing the moon and gazing at it. One then offers the incense of the moon, speaks its incantation, and says: "O King entrusted with the <term>spirituality</term>..." <note>Arabic: *ruhaniyya*. This refers to the celestial spirit or planetary essence that governs a specific heavenly body—in this case, the Moon.</note>

<column-break/>

...and his safety from those who oppose him, while he is in his <term>exaltation</term> <note>The astrological position where a planet’s influence is strongest.</note>. They slaughtered a pig and smeared its face with its blood, then burned its hair as incense. They took some of its hair, bones, blood, flesh, and gall, and placed them 

<margin>3</margin> inside that brass pig. They placed some of its gall in its ears and burned the rest of the pig, placing its ashes in a brass jar before the image of the pig. They engraved upon it the spirituality of **Saturn**. They placed a brass dome over the gate, and around 

<margin>6</margin> the dome were statues of brass knights holding spears. They made the city’s foundation out of black marble, topped with red and yellow marble. At the highest point of the city, they built a great fortress with many gates. Upon each of its gates was a statue of a large lead-lined eagle, with a knight upon it holding 

<margin>9</margin> a spear, facing outward from the city. He channeled water to its eastern gate and brought male eagles, equal in number to those statues, near to them and smeared the statues with their blood. He planted orchards, established squares, and laid out farms, vineyards, and palm groves—enough to provide for him every year 

<margin>12</margin> for ten years. The distance between this city and the city of **Memphis** <note>Arabic: *Manf*, the ancient capital of Egypt.</note> was three days' journey. It held four festivals a year, at the times when the eagle would turn as its cycle moved at its highest side. <note>original footnote (French): The *Abrégé des merveilles* (Summary of Wonders) explains that the eagle was mobile; it turned toward the four cardinal directions, staying in each position for one season of the year, and festivals were held when it changed direction.</note> When they finished 

<margin>14</margin> all of this, his soul felt secure and his heart was at peace. Eventually, a letter from Al-Walid reached him 

<margin>15</margin> from the regions of **Nubia**, ordering him to send provisions and set up markets for him. So, Awn sent all of that to him in ships and on the backs of animals. He gathered his family and the daughters of the 

<margin>17</margin> kings of Egypt whom he had chosen. When Al-Walid’s entry into Egypt drew near, Awn moved to the city and fortified himself within.

### On Magic and Invisibility

...magic and invisibility. <note>The text likely refers to a specific invocation here.</note> I ask you by the One who grants you support in this matter, that you grant me what I desire from that which has been made within your power. Then take the blood and mix it 

<margin>3</margin> with the gall of the aforementioned rabbit. Bury the body in the earth immediately and hide it; do not 
reveal it. If you leave it for another day and the sun rises upon it, the **lunar spirituality** <note>Arabic: *ruhaniyyat al-qamar*. In medieval Arabic occultism, this refers to the celestial influence or "spirit" associated with the Moon.</note> will destroy you. 
Keep that blood mixed with the gall with you. When you desire invisibility, go out 

<margin>6</margin> during the hour of the Moon, take some of that blood, and smear it on your face while reciting the words of the Moon. 
Then, no one shall see you, and you may do as you wish. When you wish to be seen, stop the recitation, 
wash your face, and rub the space between your eyebrows with the aforementioned brain marrow that you have kept 

<margin>9</margin> and guarded so that no one may see it. Then say: "O spiritual being, reveal me 
and let me appear to humans like myself," and you will appear instantly. This is among their 
**lunar works**.

<margin>12</margin> Along with the mention of this work, he brought a report which I shall mention to you: a foreign man 
from the Kurds <note>The text uses *a'jam*, meaning a non-Arab, specifically identifying him as Kurdish.</note> sought out a Babylonian sage and said to him, "O master, I wish for you to teach me magic." 
The Shaykh asked him, "What is your religion?" He replied, "I am currently a follower of the religion of the Messiah." 

<margin>15</margin> The Shaykh said, "Then perform for me what the Messiah used to do in terms of raising the dead." The youth replied, "I do not know how to do 
that." The Shaykh said, "Then how are you to learn magic?" The youth asked, "Was it magic that 
Jesus performed?" The Shaykh replied, "Was it without knowledge that he did that?" The youth said, "Inform me, 

<margin>18</margin> out of your favor, regarding what I asked you." The Shaykh said, "Yes; the newborn is born in such a way, and he grows and becomes great..."

<margin>3</margin> with your hand upon your hand such and such." The youth wrote with his hand upon his hand. When he finished, the Shaykh said to him, 
"Look at what you have written in your hand." He looked and was **bewitched** <note>Arabic: *suhira*. This can mean both literally enchanted or falling into a deep, illusory trance.</note> for a long time. When he recovered, the Shaykh asked him, 
"What is the matter with you, and what has befallen you?" The youth replied, "I do not know." The Shaykh said, "You do 

<margin>6</margin> not even know what we intended for you through the writing in your hand; how then can you expect to learn a science where you have not even reached a minute detail of it?" 
The youth was dumbfounded and began turning his palms over, falling into a trance for a long time. When he recovered, the Shaykh said to him, 
"What is the matter with you, and what has befallen you?" The youth said, "I have repented, so release me." The Shaykh said to him, 

<margin>9</margin> "Release yourself, O you who are ignorant of yourself! You have no portion in the science of magic." The youth was stunned and turned 
his face toward the wall. There, he saw **statues** <note>Arabic: *tamathil*. These are likely wall-reliefs or magical animated figures.</note> that were opposing one another: one intended 
to burn his companion with fire, while the other met him with water; one desired to stand up, while another destroyed what was 

<margin>12</margin> beneath him to prevent him from standing. The Shaykh said to him, "What do you see?" The youth told him what he saw. 
The Shaykh said to him, "He who understands the science..." The youth remembered and wiped what was on his hand before looking at it. 
The Shaykh said to him, "Renounce this, O man! For this is a science from which you are far removed."

of his mount, which was brought to Alexander. When the man saw his mount and recognized it, he said,

And they said: The wood breaks and the rope snaps.
And they said: The beginning of thought is the end of action. <note>A philosophical maxim: the final result achieved in reality is the first thing conceived in the mind.</note> An example of this is when wood is moved; the wood is moved by the wind, and fire is moved by **mechanical motion** <term>al-haraka al-handasiyya (literally "geometrical movement")</term> upon water, wind, or mercury.

### Chapter (4)

We have extracted for you, O observer, from the "eyes" <note>meaning the choice selections or essence</note> of the books of these people regarding this matter, that which, if you reflect upon it, you will realize the extent of the hardship we endured in gathering it from their scattered writings. These are the foundations of this matter. Among them is what **Mercury the Babylonian** <note>Arabic: *Utarid al-Babili*. In this tradition, the planet Mercury is often personified as a sage or identified with Hermes Trismegistus.</note> mentioned in his "Chapters," which he titled **"The Secret of Secrets"** <note>Arabic: *Sirr al-Asrar*. A famous medieval treatise on statecraft and the occult, often attributed to Aristotle or Hermes.</note>. We have summarized forty-five chapters from it containing much of the knowledge we are pursuing.

(1) The first of them is his saying: **Attuning oneself to the planet** <note>original: *al-tatabb'u bi-l-kawkab*</note> is an aid to whoever persists in it for the sake of drawing down its powers.
(2) Ask the **Sun** for the greatness of awe, the loftiness of character, the height of ambition, the dominion over tyrants, the humbling of sultans, the kindling of fires, and the illumination of darkness.
(3) Ask the **Moon** for the facilitation of movements, the revealing of secrets, the various types of waters, the extinguishing of fires, the undoing of firmly settled matters, and the scattering of unified desires.

(١٤) If you are able to use a **fixed star** <term>al-kawkab al-thabit (stars that do not move relative to each other)</term> of the same nature as each **wandering planet** <term>al-kawkab al-mutahayyir (the five visible planets plus the Sun and Moon)</term>, you will combine the power of influence with the permanence of the work.
<margin>3</margin> (١٥) If the **Ascendant** <term>al-tali‘ (the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon)</term> is of the same nature as the need and the ruling planet, and you seek help from a fixed star and your conviction is sound, the goal is made easy and the influence strong.
(١٦) One may seek help from the **Flying Eagle** <note>Altair (al-Nasr al-Ta'ir), the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.</note> for movement, just as one seeks help from the **Falling Eagle** <note>Vega (al-Waqi‘), the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.</note> for stillness.

(٢٠) Seek refuge with the Sun when someone is humbled <note>original: "dhallat" (to be humbled). Variants suggest this refers to rituals for overcoming or subjugating an opponent.</note>, for that leads to correction, increase, and the swiftest response.

(٢٤) Seek help from **Mars** if you are overpowered, for its influence is more piercing and its response swifter in this matter than others; it leads to rectification and increase.

(٢٥) Seek help from **Venus** if you are weary, for her influence is stronger and her response swifter in this matter than others; she leads to rectification and increase.

(٢٦) Seek refuge with **Mercury** if you are ignorant, for in that he leads to rectification and increase, being more piercing in influence and swifter in response.

(٢٧) Slowness of response stems from your own dregs <note>The Arabic term *daraki-ka* is obscure; scholars suggest it refers to personal impurities or "dregs" that hinder spiritual reception.</note>, or from weakness of certainty, or from poor arrangement of the ritual.

(٢٨) The work performed by establishing **incenses** <term>al-dukhnat (ritual fumigations used to attract spirits)</term> and the recitation of **invocations** <term>al-da‘wat (formal petitions)</term> is superior to work performed by rising vapors and varying breaths <note>This likely refers to internal meditative practices or simpler breathing exercises compared to full ceremonial ritual.</note>.

(٢٩) The rising of the Sun and the falling of gazes <note>i.e., the presence of observers or daylight.</note> cuts off the spiritual powers of the **nocturnal planets**.

(٣٠) The darkness of night and the stillness of movement cuts off the spiritual powers of the **diurnal planets**; therefore, use every planet in its proper turn.

(٣١) A heavy planet <term>al-kawkab al-thaqil (the outer planets like Saturn and Jupiter, which move slowly)</term>, by its stillness, is more piercing in influence than a light planet <term>al-kawkab al-khafif (the Moon or Mercury, which move quickly)</term> by its motion, even if they are equal in power.

(٣٢) Do not ask **Mars** for affinity <note>Mars is the planet of war and separation, not harmony.</note>, just as you do not ask **Venus** for estrangement; judge other matters accordingly and do not divert a planet from its natural path.

Every city built while **Mars** is at the Midheaven <note>The highest point of the sky in a birth chart, representing authority and public standing.</note> or with a fixed star of a similar nature, will find that most of those who rule over it die by the sword.

(8) Do not overlook the matter of the one hundred and twenty conjunctions of the **wandering planets** <note>original: *al-kawakib al-mutahayyira* (the planets), so-named because they appear to move against the backdrop of the "fixed" stars.</note>, for in them lies the knowledge of most things that happen in the world of **generation and corruption** <term>al-kawn wa-l-fasad (the material world where things are born, change, and decay)</term>.

(9) In every judgment, act according to the capacity of the recipient to accept the full form of the action <note>A warning that astrological magic only works if the target is naturally capable of receiving that specific influence.</note>.

(10) The **Sun** is the fountain of the animal power <note>The "vital spirit" or life force that allows movement.</note>, the **Moon** is the fountain of the natural power, **Saturn** is the fountain of the retentive power <note>The ability of the body or mind to hold onto things.</note>, **Jupiter** is the fountain of the power of growth, **Mercury** is the fountain of the intellectual power, **Mars** is the fountain of the irascible <note>Assertive or anger-driven energy.</note> and attractive powers, and **Venus** is the fountain of the concupiscent <note>Desire-driven or appetitive.</note> power. For this reason, **Mercury**, **Mars**, and **Venus** in a birth chart are the primary indicators of a person's character and their profession.

I have seen words by the illustrious **Plato** in some of his philosophical compositions that are fitting to mention here. Among them is his saying: "Nothing points toward truths except **Jupiter**."

Also his saying: "Just as the elements of the human body are blood, the two biles <note>Yellow bile and black bile, parts of the four classical "humors."</note>, and phlegm, so too are the elements of the powers within the body the wandering planets. The dominance of one over the other depends on the placement, strength, or weakness of the wandering planets at the moment of one's beginning."

And his saying: "That which prevents the science of the stars from being explicit..." <note>The text here is fragmentary or unclear in the original manuscript.</note>

<page-num>325</page-num>

(1) The astrologer can repel many of the stars' effects if he knows the nature of that which is being affected, and prepares a receptive vessel <note>original: *qabilan* (a recipient or material subject).</note> to endure the action before it occurs.

(2) The wise soul assists the celestial action just as the farmer assists the powers of nature through plowing and weeding.

(3) The forms in the **world of composition** <note>The physical, material world made of combined elements.</note> are obedient to the celestial forms. For this reason, the makers of **talismans** <term>al-tilasmat (objects created to capture and store the power of specific stars)</term> drew them when the planets resided in those forms, according to what they intended to achieve.

(4) Use the **malefics** <term>al-nuhus (literally "the unfortunates," referring to Mars and Saturn)</term> in **elections** <term>al-ikhtiyarat (the branch of astrology used to choose the best time to start a project)</term> just as a skilled physician uses poisons—in exactly the right dosage.

(5) The agreement between two people on a matter is derived from the indicator of that matter in their respective **birth charts** <term>al-mawalid (nativities)</term>. If the indicators are of a single likeness, there will be agreement between them. The one with the stronger planetary position takes the role of the agent and leader, while the weaker takes the role of the recipient and the led.

(6) Love and hatred are determined by the exchange of positions of the **two luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> in their birth charts, and the similarity of their **ascendants** <term>al-tawali‘ (the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth)</term>. The "obedient sign" <note>A technical term for signs that share the same amount of daylight, suggesting harmony.</note> indicates the strongest love.

(7) Use the **fixed stars** for the building of cities and the **wandering planets** for the building of houses.

# The Secrets of the Philosophers and the Science of Talismans

The celestial sciences were addressed by a group of philosophers—namely Grotius <note>Original: *Kurūtiyūs*. This name likely refers to a Greek figure, possibly Critias or a corruption of another Neoplatonic authority; the Latin version of this text, the *Picatrix*, omits these specific names.</note>, Philemon, Agathodaemon <note>A legendary figure in Hermetic literature, often identified as a teacher of Hermes Trismegistus.</note>, and those like them. Their speech on the matter was obscure and their symbols were hidden. Consequently, the ambiguity within their compositions led to a failure <margin>3</margin> in reaching the desired goal and a lack of success. Thus, the potential for harm grew alongside the very benefit for which the works were composed.

In this craft, I have provided hints that will not be hidden from the intelligent adept or the brilliant philosopher. The first gateway into it is knowing the forms of the rising stars and understanding those forms which exist <margin>6</margin> by themselves, as well as knowing those forms where no part appears until it is combined with members of another. One then attempts to imprint their nature into earthly clay <term>al-ṭīna al-arḍiyya</term> in accordance with the celestial primematter <term>al-hayūlā al-samāwiyya</term>.

One must intuit and seek out—within the lower clay of common animals—that which corresponds <margin>9</margin> to the common spiritual forms within those celestial images. One seeks that which is most closely attached and most suitable in spirit to those forms, in order to achieve a true homogenization and to imprint the shape through correspondence. This is done in pursuit of the "conjugation" <note>The union of the celestial spirit with the material object.</note> which, in this craft, is the foundation of the Hyleg <term>al-haylāj (the astrological "Giver of Life" that determines the lifespan of a person or an object)</term>.

If you do this, the <margin>12</margin> talisman will stand with eternal stability and perpetual existence in the purpose for which it was intended. Its power will not end until the clay itself vanishes, the composition decays, or its status is lost—though sometimes its power ends because the lifespan of the planet's influence expires. 

The best foundation upon which a talisman can be imprinted is the action of the seven wandering planets. The most enduring and <margin>15</margin> highest of these actions occurs when a benefic planet <note>A "Fortunate" planet, usually Jupiter or Venus, believed to bring positive influence.</note> faces the talisman, assisting in the descent of its spirituality from the celestial sphere to the Earth. 

Sometimes, among the Divine Names, there are those which, if used to draw down spirituality, cause it to descend and fall low. These names might even kill the practitioner if he is not knowledgeable in the nature of the planetary spirituality he is summoning.

<column-break/>

...the variation in the response of the recipient. For this reason, the calculations of the practitioner of omens and augury often fluctuate. He <margin>3</margin> works on the assumption that a specific result is coming, but perhaps he encounters something that suits him, or perhaps something else entirely arrives.

Among the words of **Hippocrates**, the leader in this field, is this concise saying: "When Jupiter <note>Original: *al-Burjīs*, an ancient name for the planet Jupiter.</note> overcomes the Sun at the time of the Solar Revolution <note>The moment the Sun returns to its exact position at the time of a birth or an event, used for yearly predictions.</note>, the year will have <margin>6</margin> few illnesses and much health, and it will be favorable for pregnancy and childbirth."

From the words of the wise **Aristotle**: "Sovereignty belongs to **Saturn**, Justice to **Jupiter**, Elegance to **Venus**, Governance to **Mercury**, Service to **the Moon**, and Tyranny to **Mars**."

We have brought you these collective sayings of these people from their various books so that you may know that, despite their brilliant <margin>9</margin> insight and their advancement in the sciences, their only concern was the extraction of these secrets—expressed as "The Two Results" <note>likely referring to the dual outcomes of spiritual enlightenment and material mastery</note>—and the attainment of them.

**Ishaq ibn Hunayn** <note>A famous 9th-century translator who brought Greek science and philosophy into the Arabic world.</note> also translated a treatise by **Aristotle**, the true Master <margin>12</margin> of the Greeks and the one most deserving of merit and precedence. I have seen fit to record it for you in this place so that you may understand all the words of these people, the depths of their thoughts, and the results of their intellects. We had previously mentioned some excerpts <margin>15</margin> in the first treatise, but a spiritual consensus was later reached to record it in its entirety because of its small size.

The first point is that for every craft there is a door through which the seeker enters, and a ladder by which the climber ascends. For he who rides upon matters recklessly, overstepping them with risk, cuts himself off and fails to <margin>18</margin> reach his desire. 

This science is among the divine gifts and the celestial grants...

->## On the Integrity of the Craft and the Measure of the Heavens<-

Know that one who crafts a talisman for purposes other than the wandering stars <note>Original: *al-sayyārah*, the planets.</note> is merely a reckless agitator seeking discord and eager for corruption. Keep your distance from such a person. Observe what he faces when erecting the talisman: whatever is <margin>3</margin> manifest in the celestial sphere, manifest it; whatever is concealed, conceal it; and whatever is hidden, give it weight. God—Mighty and Majestic—is the Giver of His bounty and the Guardian of His wisdom. This is the literal text of his words. So, train yourself, O observer, and pay heed to the secrets he has deposited in this result. Look at his statement: if you desire the duration of <margin>6</margin> the talisman’s existence to be eternal, how should one use the degree of the beginning of the circle of horizons? For that is what separates the visible half of the sphere from the hidden half.

Know—may God enlighten your mind—that the "degree" is a specific quantity used in estimation, though it is one <margin>9</margin> of those terms with multiple meanings. The astronomical degree <term>al-daraja al-falakiyya</term> is sixty-six and two-thirds miles. The "degree" is also used regarding qualities—meaning heat, cold, moisture, and dryness—where estimation is applied to anything that can be measured in its entirety by one or more of its parts. Likewise, the "minute" <margin>12</margin> <term>al-daqīqa</term> is five parasangs <note>A *farsakh* (parasang) is an ancient unit of distance, roughly 3 to 3.5 miles.</note>, four-fifths of a parasang, and one-sixtieth. The mile is three thousand spans <term>bā‘</term>, the span is three cubits <term>dhirā‘</term>, the cubit is two hand-spans <term>shibr</term>, and the hand-span is two thumb-spans <term>fatar</term>.

There was an urgent need to acquaint you with these nuances and the knowledge of what the astronomical <margin>14</margin> degree truly is. Reflect, may God honor you, upon these noble passages with which we have favored you. Conceal them <margin>15</margin> from all but those worthy of them. If you find even one person capable of grasping them, know that we have not left out any secret from those who preceded us—anything we attained, we have bestowed upon you. In this, we follow the example of the leader of this matter in his writings— <margin>18</margin> I mean the unique figure of his age, **Abu Musa Jabir ibn Hayyan** <note>The famous 8th-century polymath and alchemist known in the West as Geber.</note>. What then is your opinion of him, O...

<column-break/>

As for magical incantations <term>al-ruqā</term>, although they do not exceed the earthly circle, they approximate this craft in summoning what is summoned. However, incantations do not achieve their effect unless <margin>3</margin> the hope in them is tied to the Greatest God, who moves them by command toward the primematter <term>al-hayūlā</term> and directs them toward the center-point of the Earth.

The talisman-maker must possess prior knowledge of the essence of the prepared nature and how it is <margin>6</margin> made ready. There must be an incanter, and he must take care that there is no innate enmity between the two natures <note>The nature of the practitioner and the nature of the target.</note> or the specific image being formed. For example—and I give this example for the most observant of people—I say: if the image bound by the spirituality of the talisman is a lion, then the practitioner <margin>9</margin> who binds the talisman should not be someone who suffers from intense fear of this animal in his natural temperament. He should have seen a lion and known how to repel its aggression—perhaps with fire, as they mentioned, or with the image of a rooster <margin>12</margin> as they claimed. He should prepare one of these two things during the binding. If the maker possesses these qualities, he will be a ruler whose desires are carried out. God, Great and Majestic, knows that I have never seen this mentioned by any ancient philosopher.

To complete the power of the talisman's influence, you must assemble it during the agitation of its form and the peak of its kind. <margin>15</margin> You must take care that this does not occur during an ailment afflicting the one who imprints or the one being imprinted upon, for that would weaken its action. Every circular movement in the heavens is a movement that stirs that specific animal on <margin>18</margin> Earth by the decree of the Subtle Creator. Observe the cycle of that planet: if you intend for the talisman's duration to be eternal, two forms are made for it. One is from the degree that is the beginning of its <margin>21</margin> crossing through the zodiac, and the second is from its departure toward its resting place. Thus, whenever it revolves in its sphere, the power of the talisman revolves with it—coming and going, ascending and descending.

Conversely, if we wish to expel snakes and wasps, we use the Kark-stone <note>original: *al-kark*; likely a type of jasper or hematite used in medieval lapidaries to repel pests</note>, magnetite, silver, and similar stones. Some of the predecessors in the study of stones chose to use the diamond <margin>3</margin> for all such purposes, which is an elegant opinion. However, if the animal is of a "cold" nature—such as the scorpion, the fly, the gnat, the louse, and their like—then the stone used against it must be "hot," such as malachite <term>al-dahnaj</term>, copper, gold, <margin>6</margin> alum <term>al-shabba</term>, and the like. This applies to destruction and expulsion.

As for acquisition and attraction, <margin>6</margin> one must use similarity <note>The "Law of Similitude" suggests that like attracts like.</note>. For animals like snakes, one uses gold, copper, and the remaining [hot] materials. For scorpions, one uses the Kark-stone, crystal, and the like. The reason for this is the harmony of temperaments and the alignment <margin>9</margin> of proper movements, versus the discord of temperaments and the divergence of individual movements that are contrary to the [intended] path.

As for engravings and schematic images, they should follow the likeness of the animal: a mouse for a mouse, <margin>12</margin> snakes for snakes, vipers for vipers, a scorpion for a scorpion, and a gnat for a gnat. Know that the physical size of a talismanic stone is small and a minor part of its function; while the stone used for engraving may <margin>12</margin> weigh only between an ounce and a pound, the reach of its effect can extend for a hundred parasangs <note>A *farsakh* (parasang) is roughly 3 miles, making this a range of 300 miles.</note> or more or less. However, that extension is either through the composite nature [of the talisman] or its essence. For that which is firmly rooted has no movement <margin>15</margin> or action beyond its immediate location—like the elements of earth and water—while the reach of spirits <term>al-arwāḥ</term> is wider than the place of small-spirited bodies.

Observe, O viewer, the saying of Plato when he said: "Bodies are the opposites of <margin>15</margin> souls; this one cannot flourish unless that one is in ruin. Therefore, prefer the ruin of your bodies for the flourishing <margin>18</margin> of your souls, and grant your souls authority over your desires, which are the pleasures of your bodies."

...the seeker in revealing the inner secrets of the people's wisdom <note>Refers to the "People of the Craft," the community of alchemists and sages.</note>. I mention here from his words that which will help you reach your desire, which is his saying: The work of the talisman is merely an imitation of the actions of nature. <margin>3</margin> It can only be accomplished by knowing what has been allotted to nature regarding animals, plants, and stones, as well as the alignment of the planets, fixed stars, and the zodiac signs with the regions of the earth. It requires mastery of astronomy, <margin>6</margin> the fortunes of the planets and their mansions, latitude and longitude, the natures of the earth's regions, its waters, its soil, its rains, its snows, its deserts, its seas, its rivers, and their locations relative to the equator. One must also know what animals are formed and thrive there, the duration of their lives, and all their various types, such as snakes, scorpions, gnats, mice, wasps, geckos, <margin>9</margin> humans, beasts of burden, and cattle. This is because there are regions of the earth where none of these animals are formed, and others where some are formed and others are not. Whoever knows these things will not find the crafting, derivation, and extraction of a talisman difficult.

The most reliable <margin>12</margin> talismanic work is done with stones rather than the other two kingdoms [plants and animals], because plants dry out and burn over time until they perish, and animals rot and have little endurance in their formation—though work is possible in all of them. The action of talismans is twofold: either acquisition and attraction, <margin>15</margin> or destruction and expulsion. Similarly, the times [for crafting] are twofold, and the movement is twofold. This is because the times for destruction and expulsion are the most frequently needed in the chapters <margin>18</margin> regarding the degrees [of the zodiac] and the planets. There is a secret in stones: if the nature of the animal to be expelled is hot, the stone should be cold; if it is moist, the stone should be dry.

...as the composition of the movement of the strings <note>Referring to the strings of an instrument like the oud or lyre</note> so that the movements might unite; in this lies the joy of the world and its pleasures. The memory of this harmony encompasses the world, its joy is intensely burning, and its delight is great. O <margin>3</margin> observer, apply your thought to the results of the ideas of these people. The ancient sages used to urge the <term>exercise of the souls</term> <note>original: *riyadat al-anfus*; refers to spiritual or ascetic training</note> during wakefulness and sleep. It is said: "Exercise your souls through visions, for much of what you do not perceive while awake, you shall perceive in dreams." By this saying, he meant that during <margin>6</margin> the time of wakefulness, the external senses distract the internal senses from their activities. But at the time when these [external senses] have no action, this sage commanded the use of the internal powers, such as thought, estimation <term>al-wahm</term>, memory, and opinion. For the soul at that time, when its powers are stripped [of external distraction], is not occupied by <margin>9</margin> any diverter, and the [innate] heat has become hidden. When the heat is hidden, it dissolves every excess in the body. If the soul is exercised at that time, it will manifest to you during the time of the vision and allow you to see clearly the clarification of what you were thinking about.

<margin>12</margin> ## Chapter (5)

Through diligence—may God grant you strength—and through exercise in sleep and wakefulness, these people reached what they attained in perceiving the two lofty results after mastering the <term>Ten Sciences</term>. Five of these <margin>15</margin> are necessary to be known by the "Lawgivers" <note>original: *wad'i al-nawamis*; those who establish divine or civic laws</note>, and five of them are necessary to be known by the philosopher. <margin>(1)</margin> The first of these is the science of agriculture, animal husbandry, and navigation <note>original: *al-falaha wa al-ri'aya wa al-milaha*</note>. These are needed in the <margin>17</margin> initial state for the founding of cities and their proper cultivation. For this, prior knowledge and advanced science are indispensable, and books on these subjects have been composed.

<page-num>٣٣٢</page-num>

...so that the bodies might be the tools of the souls in their will. Do not make your spirits tools for your bodies. Put to death the "dead" of the two groups with the life of the "living," and do not put to death the "living" with the death of the "dead." <margin>3</margin> Remember when a sage was asked: "O Wise One, why does the soul feel delight at the movement of the strings?" He replied: "Because nature moves the reckless impulses of the Rational Soul <term>al-nafs al-mantiqiyya</term> and the Animal Soul <term>al-nafs al-bahimiyya</term> through a natural, apparent likeness—which is like a body to it—according to the order of love <margin>6</margin> and dominance present in the soul. Sometimes it unifies the parts, and sometimes it multiplies the unity. When nature moves with a continuous movement—meaning the connection of parts—the two souls embrace in spiritual love and connect with the radiant visions <margin>8</margin> of its likeness, becoming subtle and simple. But when it moves them with a disjointed movement, the Animal Soul drags it toward corporeal love. Likewise, regarding the limit of dominance: <margin>10</margin> the Rational Soul feels delight and takes mastery through the subtle likeness required by nature. But the Animal Soul feels delight in the divided parts and strings toward the divided likeness <margin>12</margin> of the body of nature. This is because the soul has within itself forms that it cannot manifest through speech <term>al-mantiq</term> toward nature. So, when nature moves it with the likeness of the "body" it possesses—meaning the bodies of the strings and their weights—the soul feels delight at the movement of those forms which it was unable <margin>15</margin> to express through speech. Thus, the soul moves them through forms and subtle movement of the eyebrow, the pupil of the eye, the smile, and other members of the body. For this reason, it is said <margin>17</margin> that the sound of the string is the link between the impressions of nature and the soul. <margin>9</margin> while the beloved does not love them back.

### The Instruments of Generation

The organs and their forms are produced, and the semen is the instrument of the male. Instruments are of two kinds: some are **detached** and others are **attached**. For example, in the case of a doctor, the hand is an instrument that treats just as a scalpel does, yet the hand is an **attached instrument**, 
<margin>3</margin> while the medicine is a **detached instrument**. The doctor only "attaches" to the medicine at the moment he acts or prepares it. Through careful management, the doctor imparts a "mediated power" <note>original: *quwa mufada*; a power or influence transferred from an agent to a subject</note> to the medicine, which then moves the body of the sick person toward health. Once that power is received, the doctor places it within the patient’s body, and at that moment, the body begins to move toward health. 
<margin>6</margin> Whether the doctor who delivered that power is alive or dead, the process continues. Similarly, both the semen and the scalpel are instruments that do not perform their function except through the connection to the practitioner using them. However, the hand is more "attached" to the practitioner than the scalpel. 

As for medicine, it works by the power within it without the doctor needing to remain **attached** 
<margin>9</margin> to it. In this same way, the semen is an instrument of the male, but the "generative power" is **detached**, much like the medicine is detached from the doctor. However, the seminal vessels and the testicles <term>al-unthayayn</term> <note>literally "the two feminine ones," a common medieval Arabic term for the testicles</note> are instruments of generation that are **attached** to the body, just as the doctor's hand is attached to his body.

Know that masculinity is an **active power** in both plants and animals. 
<margin>12</margin> In animals, masculinity is found in one individual and femininity in another. In plants, however, masculinity and femininity are often found together, joined perfectly in a single individual, such as in many plants 
that are produced from seeds. In these cases, the plant provides the "matter"—which is the seed—and provides 
<margin>15</margin> along with it the "reception of form" and a power by which it moves toward that form as well. That which provides the readiness to receive the form is the **feminine power**, and that which provides the principle of movement toward the form is the **masculine power**. There are some animals that function in this same way. There are also animals 
<margin>18</margin> in which the feminine power is complete, but it is joined by a deficient masculine power that only performs its function to a certain extent before it fails. In such cases, it requires an external aid, such as birds that lay "wind-eggs" <note>original: *yabid bi-al-rih*; eggs produced without fertilization, thought in antiquity to be caused by the wind</note> or many species of fish that lay their eggs, and then the male encounters them and casts...

<column-break/>

...one of them provides the **matter** from which the animal possessing that power is formed, and the other 
provides the **form** of that species of animal and moves the matter until that 
<margin>3</margin> **form** is perfected. The power that provides the matter is the female power, and the power that provides the form is the male power. The female is female by virtue of the power with which she prepares the matter, and the male is male by the power that 
gives that matter the form of the species to which that power belongs. The organ that serves 
<margin>6</margin> the heart by preparing the matter in the female is the **womb**, and the organ that serves the heart by providing the form is the male organ, which contains the semen. When the semen enters the womb and encounters the blood there, which the 
womb has prepared to receive the human form, the semen gives that blood a power by which it moves 
<margin>9</margin> until the organs of the human and the form of every limb—and the overall human form—are created from that blood. 

Thus, the blood prepared in the womb is the "matter" of the human, and the semen is the "mover" of that 
matter until the form is realized within it. The relationship of the semen to the blood prepared in the womb is like the relationship 
<margin>12</margin> of **rennet** <term>al-infaha</term> <note>original: *al-infaha*; the substance used to curdle milk into cheese. Medieval thinkers used this to explain how semen acts as a catalyst without becoming part of the physical body of the fetus.</note> to the milk it curdles. The rennet is the agent of the curdling, but it is not 
part of the curdled substance, nor is it its matter. Similarly, the semen is not a physical part of the fetus formed in the womb, 
nor is it the matter. The fetus is formed from the semen in the same way that yogurt is formed from rennet, 
<margin>15</margin> and it is formed from the blood of the womb just as a pitcher is formed from copper. 

That which produces the semen in humans 
are the vessels in which the semen is found; these are the veins located beneath the skin of the pubic area, and the testicles provide 
some assistance in this. These veins lead to the passage within the 
<margin>18</margin> penis <term>al-qadib</term>, and the semen flows from those veins into the passage of the penis, and flows through that passage 
until it is poured into the womb, giving the blood within it a principle and a power by which it changes until...

The time for their operation is the speech involving the binding of the spiritual forces <term>ruhaniyyat</term> <note>Spiritual entities or celestial energies associated with the planets</note> through their specific invocations, performed in solitude and isolation. At the time of their operation, no one should share in the work but you. These are the general incenses upon which the sages of 
<margin>3</margin> India relied for public interests and shared goals. Through such means, wonders were produced by them—derived from heavenly decrees and spiritual works.
It is established in the "Torah of Moses" (peace be upon him) with the following text:
> "And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: 'O Moses, proceed and take choice spices; specifically, take 500 *mithqals* <term>mithqal</term> <note>a unit of weight, approximately 4.25 grams</note> of pure, 
<margin>6</margin> fragrant myrrh, and of fragrant, sweet-smelling cinnamon half as much—that is 250 *mithqals*—and of sweet cane <note>likely *calamus*</note> the same amount as the cinnamon, and of choice cassia the same amount. Let this be according to the shekel of the sanctuary <note>original: *mithqal al-quds*</note>, the value of which is twenty dirhams. Take also a *hin* <term>hin</term> <note>a liquid measure, approximately 5 liters</note> 
<margin>9</margin> of fresh, bitter olive oil. Make it into a holy anointing oil. Let the purification of 
anointing be in the Tabernacle <note>original: *qubbat al-zaman*, literally "Dome of Time"</note>, the Ark of the Testimony, the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its vessels, 
and all these places.'" This is the text from the Torah of Moses (peace be upon him). We have provided it to you only so that you may learn 
<margin>12</margin> the secret of these people.

And in it also is this text:

finely ground, salted, pure and holy for the sanctuary. Burn some of it in the Tabernacle before the Ark.'"

## **Incense of Mars**
As for the mixtures for blending the spiritual nature of Mars Above with the Below, they are as follows:
Take thirty *mithqals* each of red asafoetida <term>hiltit</term> <note>a pungent resin used in medicine and magic, often associated with "maleficent" planets</note>, mustard, and butter. 
<margin>3</margin> Take two *mithqals* each of sagapenum <term>sakbinaj</term> <note>a yellow-brown resin from a Persian plant, similar to galbanum</note> and red arsenic. Take ten *mithqals* each of the dried brains of sparrows 
and hedgehogs. Take twenty *mithqals* 
of dried tiger <note>the Arabic *numur* may refer to leopards or panthers</note> blood, and five *mithqals* of the fat of red snakes. Combine all of these into tablets after 
<margin>6</margin> drying, grinding, sifting, and binding the powers together. Set it aside until the time of need. One must protect these 
incenses from the eyes of men and from the light of the sun or moon falling upon them. Store them 
in a shielded, preserved place, inside pyxes <note>small boxes</note> made of the metal belonging to the planet 
<margin>9</margin> associated with that incense. Let the work be linked together, one part to the next. Beware of neglecting 
any of the subtle details of these matters, for you would fail in what you attempt, and perhaps its harm might even return upon you. I shall mention 
later how to repel the hostility of these works.

## **Incense of Mercury**
As for the mixtures of the incense of Mercury: Take 
<margin>12</margin> ten *mithqals* each of camel grass flowers <term>idhkhir</term> <note>a fragrant medicinal grass</note>, 
malabathrum leaves <note>leaves of the *Cinnamomum tamala* tree</note>, and asarabacca <note>wild ginger</note>. Take two *mithqals* each of ambergris and 
castoreum <term>jundabadustur</term> <note>a scent gland secretion from beavers</note>. Take one *mithqal* of blue vitriol <note>or "blue coal"</note>. 
<margin>15</margin> Take ten *mithqals* each of the brains of magpies, hoopoes, and turtles. Take 
thirty *mithqals* of the blood of domestic donkeys. Combine the mixtures after grinding, sifting, and drying the brains 
and blood. Form them into tablets as we stipulated before. The wisdom in this is that your efforts shall not flag.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the occult properties of plants, transitioning from general alchemical preparations into a specific narrative and ritual involving the Laurel tree, attributed to the "Nabataean" tradition.</meta>

The sages related a long story regarding the **Laurel tree**. They mention that it spoke to a watchman. It is said that an ancient farmer was sleeping in the middle of an orchard surrounded by four trunks of Laurel trees. He saw in his dream one of the trees saying to him: "O man, is there anything in this orchard of yours better than me? Or who can say they have seen my like?" 

The watchman asked, "What is the meaning of this?" 

She replied, "You must recognize my merit over all other trees and my high standing with **Jupiter** <note>original: "al-Mushtari," the planet associated with growth, kingship, and divine favor</note>. Show me kindness by tending to my growth and watering. Rise at midnight with a little **wallflower oil** <term>dehn al-khiri</term> <note>A fragrant oil derived from the wallflower plant, often used as a base in medieval perfumery and talismans</note> and anoint me with it. Then raise your head toward the sky, look at Jupiter, and say: 'O **Luck of Lucks** <note>original: "Sa'd al-Su'ud," the name of a specific star in the constellation Aquarius, considered highly auspicious</note>, add fifteen years to my life starting now.' You may be certain that you will live them from that moment, provided you say: 'I seek intercession with you through this tree.' Try this, O man, and you will find it true; you will benefit yourself and recognize my merit and status with Jupiter." 

Thus, the Laurel was named "The Speaker to the Watchman" and also "Who Has Seen My Equal?" **Ibn Wahshiyya** <note>A 10th-century scholar famous for translating "The Nabataean Agriculture," a work that preserves ancient Mesopotamian botanical lore mixed with magic</note> claimed that within these words lies great knowledge and a successful symbol of the properties inherent in this tree.

### Page 354

...a status in his actions, benefits, and harms. However, despite this, he is a crafty deceiver whose evil is unbearable and whose strength cannot be resisted. Therefore, we seek protection from his evil. He is not the opposite of the **Marshmallow** <term>Khatmī: The Althaea officinalis or Hollyhock, personified here as a rational being</term>; rather, they are both in agreement in a single nature of coldness, heaviness, and slowness. Both are attributed to two powerful planets: **Mercury** <note>original: "'Atārid"</note> and his father **Saturn** <note>original: "Zuhal"</note>. 

These two plants are both rational. We were surprised that evil broke out between them, since disputes and evils usually occur between two fools. As for two rational beings, how rare it is for evil to occur between them! This is because rational beings do not have evil occur between them except for a compelling reason that necessitates the occurrence of evil due to the action of an agent who <gloss>acts</gloss> upon them. As for two fools, evil comes from within them and because of them. 

Since rational beings have only one way for evil and dispute to occur, while the ignorant have two causes, that which occurs from two causes is more frequent than that which occurs from one. We have judged in favor of the **Mandrake** <term>Yabrūḥ: The Mandragora plant, famous for its human-like root and use in magic</term> because of our frequent use of him; he is a powerful aid to our work. We only use the Marshmallow in certain places, certain states, and certain matters—such as for connection, love, and profound affection, and in some talismans that are purely for benefit. As for the Mandrake, his work in evil is more potent.

I brought the letter to the Marshmallow tree and informed her of its arrival. Then I departed, and she came to me in my sleep. I told her of the judgment, and she said: 

"They have judged for me against him, not for him against me, by their saying that I am 'good' and he is 'evil,' and by their saying that they only praise and prefer him for his 'evil.' The proof of my statement is that every evil animal that is feared among the beasts, such as lions and various types of snakes, is terrifying because of its evil, and they are...

<column-break/>

### Page 355

...miserable and exhausted, while the good ones that eat grass are fortunate. For this reason, the snake is hunted and killed, while fish and turtles are protected and safe. They have judged him as evil and fearsome, while I am better and more fortunate, just as the good among the children of humanity are in a better state than the wicked—far better in many ways and aspects that would take too long to list. 

If there were no difference between the good and the evil except the peace of heart for the good person and the preoccupation of heart for the evil one, it would be enough. For the one with the peaceful heart finds pleasure in what he eats and drinks, while the one with the preoccupied heart never finds pleasure. <gloss>For the sake of</gloss> this, it was an oral decree of **Shifāhī** <note>A legendary sage of the "Nabataean" tradition</note>, the sage of the **Jarāmiqa** <note>An ancient people of Mesopotamia and Syria</note> among the people of his land, to depict in their temples the image of **Lord Dawānāy** <note>A deity or semi-divine figure in this tradition</note> standing, having folded the fingers of his right hand over the second <note>The text says "eighth," likely a scribal error for "second"</note> and the third, with the remaining fingers standing upright. 

He is <gloss>leaning on a branch</gloss> of a Marshmallow tree, in which are depicted the nodes that exist in the natural form of the Marshmallow's branches. A great snake is coiled around the staff, and at the top of the staff is a golden cross, with the snake opening its mouth toward the face of Dawānāy. Contained within this, according to them, is much knowledge and a magical symbol regarding the use of the Marshmallow tree and the Mandrake in **Alchemy** <term>Sīmiyā’: A branch of the occult sciences dealing with the transformation of substances or the creation of illusions</term>."

Anyone who approaches the **Rowan tree** <term>Ghubayrā: Often identified as the Service Tree or Rowan; in this context, it is treated as a plant of significant occult power</term> and takes a leaf from its highest branch, placing it upon his head like a crown while his head is exposed to the air, will experience a magnificent joy for no other reason than <margin>3</margin> the delight he finds in his heart and the rapture in his soul.

### Pages 358, 359

...weight of a pound <term>Ratl: A unit of weight, roughly equivalent to a modern pound</term>, then wrap it upon that leaf <note>original: "waraq," which can mean paper or leaves</note> which contains the lamb <note>This likely refers to the "Vegetable Lamb," a legendary plant-animal hybrid</note>. Cast upon it twenty-one flowers from **Abraham’s Tree** <term>Shajarat Ibrāhīm: The Chaste Tree (*Vitex agnus-castus*)</term>, and pour over the whole mixture four pounds of cow’s milk, specifically buttermilk. Dig a hole in moist ground to a depth of three and a half cubits, place the "purifier" vessel at the bottom, and pour donkey urine into the hole until the vessel is submerged. Leave it for an hour until the earth has absorbed the urine, then pack the soil back over it thoroughly. 

Leave it thus for forty-nine days. When you open it and bring out the vessel, you will find within it a creature in the shape of a fish, possessing two wings like those of a bat, and two eyes like those of a crab, protruding from its head. It has two hands with five fingers on each, and a tail like that of a fish. 

<margin>Do not grasp it with your hand</margin> but leave it in the vessel in the sun for one to three hours, for it will die during that time. You will know it is dead when its movement ceases. Then, leave it in the vessel and cover it with the lid for seven

days without touching it. You will then see that the body of the animal has segmented and divided. This segmentation is the sign of its reaching maturity and the state required for the intended purpose. 

The author then began to list the properties within this animal, mentioning many things. ...and filled it with pure oil, fastening its top securely. He should look into it many times every day as much as possible; this increases the light of his vision and wards off ailments from his eyelids. Let the observer be seated 
<margin>3</margin> in the shade while the vessel is placed in the sun, for this strengthens the organ <note>The eye is considered a sensitive organ that can be 'fortified' by the concentrated light reflected in the oil.</note>, repels ailments from the sight, and brings joy to his soul, success in his livelihood, and beauty in the eyes of everyone who sees him.

Another method ⁽ᵃ⁾: When the water flowing from springs decreases from its usual amount, 
<margin>6</margin> a person should take a beautiful young maiden and seat her on a high place opposite the spring. Then he should command her to play the flute <note>original: 'nay', a traditional middle-eastern end-blown flute</note> frequently and continuously, directing the flute toward the opening where the water emerges. She should do this for three hours of the day. Then let him command another maiden 
<margin>9</margin> of similar beauty and age, or close to it, to take a drum <note>original: 'tabl'</note> and beat upon it while singing the most beautiful song, while the other maiden plays the flute in rhythm with the beating of the drum. Through this, the water will increase and its quantity will grow, either immediately or after fourteen hours have passed from that time, 
<margin>12</margin> or at the same time on the following day. Let the playing of the first girl alone last three hours, and the singing of the other with the drum, flute, and rhythmic beating last six hours, so the total amount comes to 
nine hours in full. This is a powerful method for increasing the quantity of water.

Another practice ⁽ᵃ⁾: Take beautiful young virgin girls and command them to wear clothes where every one of them has a color different from the others. <margin>9</margin> times. The water will then increase significantly and clearly, either immediately or shortly thereafter.

Another [point]: ⁽ᵇ⁾ The people of India say that they must use frankincense <note>original: 'al-kundur'</note> in all their works and in every

<term>Al-Yanbu' (The Spring)</term>: A natural source of water. In this context, it is treated as a living entity that responds to the harmony of music and the visual beauty of the performers.
<term>Al-Malahi (Musical Instruments)</term>: A general term for instruments used for entertainment or ritual, here used specifically to stimulate the "spirit" of the water.
<term>Al-Kundur (Frankincense)</term>: A resin used extensively in medieval medicine and magic for its perceived ability to "clear" the brain and carry prayers to the divine.
<term>Jariya (Maiden/Young Girl)</term>: Refers to a young woman, often chosen in these rituals for her perceived purity and vital energy.
<term>Zayt (Oil)</term>: Specifically olive oil, used here as a reflective medium for ocular healing.
<term>Al-Hind (India)</term>: Frequently cited in medieval Arabic texts as a source of profound occult knowledge and superior medicinal substances.
<term>Al-Alat (Instruments)</term>: Tools or devices, here referring to the musical equipment.
<term>Al-Malaha (Beauty)</term>: The quality of elegance or comeliness required of the ritual participants to ensure success.

<margin>6</margin> Another method for killing fleas: <term>Quthami<note>The legendary sage and primary narrator of the 'Nabataean Agriculture'.</note></term> said: "What I have personally tested is to take <term>white lead<note>original: 'asfidaj', also known as ceruse.</note></term>, quicklime, and the root of the <term>squirting cucumber<note>original: 'qiththa al-himar', a medicinal plant known for its purgative properties.</note></term>; crush them and add a little foul-smelling <term>asafoetida<note>original: 'haltit', a pungent resin used in medicine and to repel pests.</note></term>. <margin>12</margin> after they have cooled. Add two <term>ounces<note>original: 'uqiyah'</note></term> to a quarter or a third of a <term>pound<note>original: 'ratl'</note></term>—this is the maximum—for every ten <term>mannas<note>original: 'amnan', a unit of weight</note></term> of wine that is turning sour or has any other type of spoilage. Leave it to settle for twenty-four hours <note>original: 'from one time to its equivalent'</note>, and the sourness will vanish from it.

...then place a piece upon the embers in the path of the wind. Indeed, the smoke of the snake cuts through the cold clouds and turns them away entirely from that place.

Another method for repelling the cold as well: three women who have <insert>recently</insert> menstruated are commanded to go out into the 
<margin>6</margin> open fields <note>original: 'sahra'</note> that are shaded by clouds threatening hail. <margin>9</margin> from those clouds.

Another method: as for what <term>Masi the Syrian<note>A historical or legendary figure cited for his expertise in agricultural magic.</note></term> mentioned, he said it is a proven method for driving away hail clouds: seven men should stand, each holding a handful of cotton. They should throw that cotton toward the clouds, 
<margin>12</margin> while accompanied by four men who clap their hands. They should raise their hands toward the clouds, clapping and shouting just as <term>ploughmen<note>original: 'akara', meaning farm laborers or peasants.</note></term> shout to drive away birds and sparrows from the crops. The more the people perform this clapping and shouting at the clouds, the more effective it is in repelling them and the faster 
<margin>15</margin> they will disperse. He said: "The clouds will pass by and bypass that place." If the number of those shouting at the clouds is increased to forty men, it is even better. Their number should not be an odd number, but rather an even one—from forty to sixty—and this has been tested.

...a small amount, it would do nothing. This was more worthy of mention in the following chapter alongside things that act by their specific properties <term>khawāṣṣ: occult or inherent properties of substances in medieval Islamic science</term>, but we mentioned it here due to its connection to what I found in the **Nabatean Accounts**. 

<a> Among these is that the plant known as **Lion's Herb** <term>Ḥashīshat al-Asad: likely a type of broomrape or a parasitic weed</term> harms the plants around it. Its specific ritual is for a young woman to bring a **white rooster with a divided comb** <note>original: "dīk afraq abyad"; a rooster with a split or double comb was often preferred in magical rituals</note> and circle around the spot, shaking the rooster until it flaps its wings. This is repeated several times, after which the herb dries up and its power is nullified. 

Do you think the herb was frightened by the rooster and thus dried up, or did it perceive something of this act? 

When **cats** <note>original: "al-sanānīr"</note> smell the scent of **spikenard** <term>Sunbul al-ṭīb: an aromatic herb used in perfumes and medicine</term>, they roll around upon it and love not to part from it because they find it so pleasant. Sometimes one of them will cry out with successive cries upon smelling it, seeking it and following it. What a wonder this is!

Among these things is the mention by **Daghrit** <note>Daghrit is an ancient sage frequently cited in this text, possibly a corruption of a Greek name like Democritus</note> that he realized during his travels through the lands of **India** and elsewhere that certain lands grow things that do not grow in others. This is true for all of them, such as the **balsam** plant in the land of **Egypt**, **ebony** in the land of the **Sudanese**, **African wood** <note>original: "al-khashab al-zanjī"; wood from the Zanj/East African coast</note> in the land of the **Zanj**, and **bananas** and **aloe** in the lands of the **Maghreb** <note>The West/North Africa</note> and other places on the same latitude in the East. Also, the **frankincense** tree <term>al-Kandar: Boswellia sacra</term> in **Shahr Oman**; if it is planted elsewhere, it does not produce in its new location. There are many other things like this which are specific to one land over another. 

This is not due to a specialty of the soil alone, but rather the agreement of the soil's nature with a certain air and the watering of a specific water. By the gathering of these elements with the nature of the earth and the specialty of the country in which it grows, its existence is perfected. The primary cause of this is the geographic latitude.

**Another method:** Squeeze as much juice as you wish from **citrons** <term>Ḥamāḍ al-utruj: the acidic juice of the citron fruit</term> and add an equal amount of **rice vinegar**. Shake it until it is mixed, then add three dirhams <note>A unit of weight, approx. 3 grams</note> of crushed **sea foam** <term>Zabad al-baḥr: likely cuttlefish bone or meerschaum</term> and **sal ammoniac** <term>al-Nushādir: ammonium chloride used in alchemy</term> for every pound of liquid. Shake it constantly for one day, then leave it in the sun for three days. Then dip whatever you wish to soften into it and place it in the hot sun until it softens and becomes like dough.

**Sulfur** softens things greatly, were it not for its offensive smell. Therefore, it is not used for any vessels used for eating, but it is used for other tasks such as **stones** and **molten bodies** <note>original: "al-ajsād al-dhā’iba"; likely referring to metals or glass</note>, for its action upon them is extraordinary.

<a> Among these, **Daghrit** said: "Why is it that if we take ten dirhams by weight of crushed **saffron**, and give it to a person to drink with **wine**, they laugh until they die? They cannot stop themselves from laughing intensely, and no one can ward off death from them. Yet, if we give them ten and a half dirhams, or nine and a half dirhams, this condition—neither the laughter nor the death—does not afflict them. What is this manifest action and influence? Is it the action of heat and other natural qualities that oppose the person's nature, or is it the action of saffron due to the specific property of the weight? For if we decrease from the ten or increase..."

...of a human or slightly more, and its leaves are like laurel leaves <term>Ghar: Laurus nobilis, the bay laurel</term>. If a person makes a wreath from it and wears it upon his head, whether he sits, walks, or goes about his work, he shall not sleep as long as that wreath <margin>3</margin> remains upon his head. Nor shall he suffer the pain of that wakefulness, and his strength is many times greater than that of others who stay awake.

In the land of the Franks <margin>6</margin> <note>original: "al-Ifranj," often referring to the French or Western Europeans; a marginal note in manuscript C1 specifically uses the Hebrew term for France</note>, there is a tree such that if a person sits beneath it for half an hour during the day, he dies. If any person touches it, or cuts a branch or a leaf from it, or even shakes it, he dies.

In the land of the Slavs <margin>9</margin> <note>original: "al-Saqāliba"; a marginal note in manuscripts C and S identifies this as Ashkenaz</note>, there is a small plant similar to some garden herbs, its leaves resembling the leaves of rue <term>Sudhāb: Ruta graveolens, a bitter medicinal herb</term>. If the root is cast exactly as it is, with its leaves and branches, after being washed of its dirt and clay, into cold water, and it remains there for an hour of the day, the water becomes as hot as fire. If the root is removed and it sits for a short while, it becomes cold again; this is a great wonder.

In the city of Rome <margin>12</margin>, there is a delicate tree that grows upon the seashore with leaves as small as chickpeas <term>Ḥimmaṣ: Cicer arietinum</term>. Its height is two cubits. Some of its leaves and branches are gathered and pressed to extract a liquid; this extract is then solidified and dried. If a weight of one and a half *dāniq* <term>dāniq: a small unit of weight, roughly 0.5 grams</term> is drunk with aged wine, it causes the drinker to have a powerful erection and he may engage in intercourse as much as he desires without fatigue <margin>15</margin>.

In the land of India, there is a plant that fire cannot burn. Also there is a tree from which a branch may be cut and cast upon the ground, whereupon it moves; it may even run as snakes run, or crawl as creeping things <margin>18</margin> crawl.

In some parts of those lands, toward the direction of the north wind, there is a tree from which sounds are heard during the season...

When the people of that island realized that this herb disappears when summer comes, they began to store it. They eat it during the summer and the rest of the year <margin>14</margin> until the herb grows again. Though it has some bitterness, they claim it still intoxicates and, along with the intoxication, it extinguishes the excessive heat that stirs within people.

<meta>This page continues the botanical survey from the "Nabatean Agriculture," moving from the strange plants of the West (France) and North (Slavic lands) to the mystical "Sun" and "Moon" trees, and the ritual uses of incense in ancient Mesopotamia.</meta>

...spring and summer, the murmur of a human. He <note>Likely referring to the ancient sage Quthami or the figure of Adam mentioned later</note> called it the **Sun Tree** and mentioned that its root is in the form of a man. All the roots of this tree take the form of a male human; there is no female form among them at all.

In the land of the Bakiyan <note>original: "al-Bākiyān"; variants in the notes suggest "al-Bākmān" or "al-Bākiyāt," possibly a mythical or distant Eastern location</note> is a tree that glows at night just as a lamp glows. If one walks near it at night, they have no need for a torch because of the abundance of its light. It is called the **Moon Tree**.

These wonders were only mentioned by **"Adam"** <note>In this tradition, Adam is often viewed as the first philosopher and recipient of agricultural revelation</note> because God revealed them to him. For this reason, he authored a book on the specific properties of plants containing a thousand leaves <note>meaning a thousand pages or folios</note>, in which are wonders regarding the **secrets of plants**.

Among the things he mentioned therein is a tree he called the **Hidden Tree**. It does not appear to anyone’s eye during the day, but it appears at night until two hours remain [before dawn], at which point it vanishes from both the sight and the touch. Its growing places are the wildernesses and deserts, and it possesses elegant wonders.

Among them is the **Costus** tree <gloss>a</gloss> <term>Qusṭ: Saussurea costus, a thistle whose roots are used for incense and medicine</term>. The variety that grows in India has the most pleasant fragrance. It is used as incense for idols and their temples. The **Chaldeans** <note>The ancient Semitic inhabitants of Mesopotamia, here associated with pagan rituals and astrology</note> say that it is the best thing to offer by burning before the idol of **Venus** <note>original: "al-Zuhra"</note>. It is used in sacrifices through which the fulfillment of needs is sought, whatever they may be. He named it "**Daghrith** the Successful" and praised it at great length. A group of them used to mix its wood with oakmoss, liquid and dry storax <term>Mīʿa: A fragrant resin from the Styrax tree</term>, rose leaves, and myrtle smeared with saffron hair.

<meta>This page continues the botanical and legendary accounts attributed to the ancient Chaldean traditions. The previous section discussed mystical trees associated with the Sun and Moon; this page narrates a specific legend involving a King, a condemned woman, and the discovery of the "Tree of Love" through the intercession of the god Jupiter.</meta>

"...that he should bring her to you, for he neither accepted your command nor killed her." The King woke up joyful and happy, and he summoned that man. The man came to him dressed in burial shrouds and embalming spices <note>Wearing burial clothes and spices signifies the man's readiness to be executed for his previous disobedience to the King's order</note>. The King said to him, "Woe to you! You have made me a partner in your guilt by failing to inform me that you did not kill so-and-so." The man replied, "O King, I only spared her because I knew of your inclination toward her. I did this seeking favor with you, even if I have erred." 

The King summoned me <note>The narrator, likely the sage Quthami</note>, and his words to me were a trial and a test. [The man continued,] "I have come to the King in shrouds and embalming spices; let him command regarding me as he wishes. If the King is pleased with my sparing her and my disobedience of his order, then I have fulfilled the King's desire in seeking favor with him." The King said, "You have indeed found favor with me, and I thank you for sparing her, because of the sorrow that struck me upon her parting and the grief over her loss. Bring her here this instant." 

So the man went and brought her. The King prostrated in joy and gratitude and ordered a grand prize for the man. The man said, "O King, I shall not depart until the King is certain that I am unfit for women." The King said, "Your status with us is far higher than that." He replied, "I shall not depart until the King tests what I have said, or he may kill me if he wishes." So the King ordered the physicians and the jurists <note>The involvement of 'jurists' suggests a formal legal verification of his physical state was required</note> to examine him. They told the King, "He is undoubtedly impotent <term>’Annin: a man who is naturally or medically unable to consummate a marriage</term>." So the King doubled his prize and ordered his dismissal. The King did not cease prostrating to the **Rabakshana Tree** for the rest of his life. He continued this throughout his reign, which lasted seventy-five years. This story became famous during that time among the **Chaldeans** <note>original: "al-Kasdaniyin"; the ancient inhabitants of Mesopotamia</note>, and they named this tree the **Tree of Love** and composed poetry about it.

He saw in his dream as if the **Rabakshana Tree** in his house—for he had a garden in one of his courtyards containing a Rabakshana tree—he saw as if that tree was addressing him, saying, "So-and-so, your wife, is alive in the world; summon so-and-so [the man] and compel him..."

<meta>This page continues the discourse on ancient agricultural and astrological wisdom. While the previous page focused on the "Tree of Love" and a specific king's mercy, this section shifts to the veneration of the planets—specifically Jupiter and Venus—and the secret botanical knowledge of the Canaanites and Chaldeans. It introduces the sage Daghrith and discusses how certain plants and incenses are used to communicate with the divine.</meta>

### Page 392 / 393

In our current time, we observe that the **Canaanites** <note>Ancient inhabitants of the Levant, often associated in these texts with deep astrological knowledge</note> show a greater veneration for **Jupiter** <note>original: "al-Mushtari"</note> than others do. Their prayers to him are more frequent, and they prefer him over other planets, believing this to be the most correct path. This difference in practice between us and them is not considered a contradiction or a schism; rather, all these paths are correct, as experience has proven the validity of both our ways and the works of the **Canaanites** and the **Chaldeans** <note>original: "al-Kasdaniyun," referring to the ancient people of Mesopotamia</note>.

The sage **Daghrith** said: "In the knowledge of plants and their associations with specific planets, there are elegant properties and hidden secrets. Through these, one can achieve great and momentous things. The ancients were stingy with this knowledge, keeping it hidden and refusing to reveal it to the common people. This was not done out of greed or a desire to withhold benefits, but to ensure that such precious science did not fall into the hands of those unworthy of it, and that only those with a plentiful and discerning intellect might grasp it."

**Abu Bakr** <note>The translator, Ibn Wahshiyya</note> stated: "**Daghrith** composed a book in which he listed plants one by one according to their planetary rank—starting with those belonging to **Saturn**, then **Jupiter**, then **Mars**, following the order of the seven planets."

Furthermore, the soul finds joy in elegant engravings and beautiful colors. Such decorations can be found on vessels, featuring various lines and curves, as well as colors—

---

2. Fil. <note>The *Fihrist* of Ibn al-Nadim</note> adds "and their veneration" after "Jupiter." | 3. V: "contradiction" instead of "conflict"; Fil: "no disagreement." | 4. Fil. omits "the Canaanites and." | 7. Scribes often wrote "thought" instead of "withheld" <note>A common phonetic slip in Arabic manuscripts: "danna" vs "zanna"</note>. | 8. C: "distributed"; Fil. adds: "This is the strongest evidence for the correctness of both views." | 10. C2 adds: "Ibn Wahshiyya" after "Abu Bakr." | 11. V: "with Saturn." | 13. —and people desired to acquire these decorated items. They became numerous in this region until the time of **King Kanur**, who forbade their acquisition and the practices associated with them. He named such things "The King’s Abomination," and so people stopped mentioning them or being infatuated with them. This was a political tactic on his part to prevent the people from worshipping these objects, as they had become excessive in their praise of them.

Among these secrets is that the wood of the **Myrrh tree** <term>Myrrh: a resinous tree used since antiquity for medicine and ritual incense</term>, when used as a fumigant, repels the plague during times of "corrupted air." It is burned as incense in temples. They also create a compound made from its wood and resin, adding to it **frankincense** <note>original: "kundur"</note>, **lichen** <note>original: "ushna"</note>, and **liquid storax** <note>original: "may'a"</note>. They call this mixture **Saqufomsa**, which in Arabic means "Delight of the Idols."

The **Canaanites** say that this incense pleases **Venus** <note>original: "al-Zuhara"</note>. They seek to draw near to her by burning it. Anyone among them who wishes to recite the incantations of **Venus** before her ritual scroll and in front of her idol must first offer this incense. They must then play the flute, beat drums, or play the lute for an hour before petitioning **Venus** for their needs. She will answer the prayer and fulfill the request, provided that she is "adorned" <note>An astrological term meaning the planet is in a favorable position</note> and her action is not blocked by another planet. Specifically, she must not be in "aspect" with **Mercury** <note>original: "Utarid"</note> nor in conjunction with him, for his influence is a stronger hindrance when he is joined with her than when he merely looks toward her.

**Daghrith** added: "If a bit of saffron and costus <note>original: "qust," an aromatic root used in ancient perfumes</note> are added to this incense, it becomes more complete and successful in fulfilling one's needs." However, the **Canaanites** did not add these and do not use them to this day.

---
